name: Israel & the Israel of God
about: Who Israel is, the church, and Zionism.

teachings.title: Romans 9: the Jews stumbled at faith
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Romans 9 is about God using nations and the unbelieving Jews' standing, not Calvinist election, and the Jews missed the promise because they sought righteousness by the law, not faith.
teachings.text:
Here Paul begins dealing with the JQ. While Calvinism uses these verses, which are about the use of nations, rulers, sinners and believers to His purpose, as being about our salvation, they do so ignoring the scriptural, Spiritual arguments that have been building throughout the epistle.

Having established God's word, His grace, our faith, the doctrine of Christ and the condition of the saved being heirs to the promise, adopted sons, he turns to explaining the unrepentant Jew's position with God, relative to the old covenant and salvation in Christ. Replacement theology is the theme. Dispies hate this.

Note what the stumblingstone preventing the Jews from being partakers of the promise; faith. They seek righteousness by the works of the law, not faith.

But WHOSOEVER believeth on Jesus Christ shall not be ashamed for trusting God's promise.

teachings.title: Stiffnecked and resisting the Holy Ghost
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Stephen's history shows Israel's constant rejection of God, so a chosen race outside Christ is fiction; God's theology never changed, only who receives His grace.
teachings.text:
The history of the Israelites, given by Stephen, which had been preached about by prophets before, by John the Baptist and by Christ Jesus, and that would be repeated in the Epistles, is a searing indictment of them as a people, and of man in general.

God pounds the message of their stiff-neckedness and disobedience, their rejection of His word, over and over again throughout the Bible. The idea of their being special or chosen as a race, outside of Christ, is unbiblical fiction. The idea of separate ethnic dispensations is a lie. "Replacement theology" itself is a misnomer, as the theology of God in scripture has remained consistent throughout, it is simply who has received the grace of God and His blessing that's changed.

teachings.title: Abraham's seed is Christ, and believers are heirs
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Believing Gentiles are Abraham's children through Christ the one seed, the law was a schoolmaster and not a separate dispensation, and no Jew, Rome or church can annul or add to God's covenant of faith.
teachings.text:
Paul asks the supposedly saved Christians of Galatia, *Received ye the Spirit by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith? He therefore that ministereth to you the Spirit, and worketh miracles among you, doeth he it by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith?* The answer is obvious to those that have the Spirit inside them, testifying to its truth. But to those still believing on their own righteousness to redeem them, this question is vexing indeed.

Quoting scripture regarding Abraham, who the Bible says in **Genesis 15:6** *And he believed in the Lord; and he counted it to him for righteousness.* This proof of our faith in God's promise of Christ Jesus being what is counted for righteousness is also quoted by Paul in **Romans 4** and in **James 2** (although to much consternation to those trusting their works to save them).

Paul reminds the Galatians that just because Jews come to tell them they need to add works of the law to their faith for salvation, that they hold no special place. That the Gentiles who received the same faith as Abraham are sons of Abraham, that all nations are blessed by Abraham's seed, that is Christ. Not seeds, plural, as in Jews after the flesh.

This chapter is also one of many nails in the coffin of dispensationalism, that wicked and often damnable heresy that places Jews in a higher regard than those that believe on Christ. The lie that they had a different way to be justified. Paul calls what they claim as a blessing, a curse.

The law was a school master, bringing those who lived under it to the understanding that no man can be justified by the works of the law. To remind them to keep the faith in the promise of God, rather than themselves. It was designed to bring them to faith, not a separate dispensation.

And of that covenant of faith, and the good news of it, no man may disannul or add to it. Read that part carefully. Understand what it means.

God made a contract with us. It is the promise of being made heirs to the Kingdom and the blessings that go along with being heirs. Being His sons. That promise only requires believing on Him to deliver on it.

Those who say they can take away your role in the promised kingdom, or adding requirements to receive it, who seek to annul or add to the covenant of God given in his testament, are liars. They can't.

Jews, Catholic church, the daughters of it, etc...cannot take away your salvation or add obedience to their traditions to receive the inheritance of faith given to Abraham, and promised by God to whosever believe. It isn't possible. They have no authority to change a covenant, a contract, given by God.

Paul says the law given to the Hebrews through Moses by God Himself didn't have the power to disannul the covenant He made with Abraham. Imagine having the hubris to think some institution of man could!

The law wasn't given to give life, but to condemn so we could understand we needed righteousness by faith.

Scripture says that God made a promise to Abraham, that faith in that promise justifies, that justification by the law is only possible by obeying the whole of it, that this is impossible, that if we place our faith in our ability to do the whole of the law, we becomes slaves to it, and that we all fall short, making the law a curse. But that in grace, we are saved by faith in Christ. Summarized:

*But the scripture hath concluded all under sin, that the promise by faith of Jesus Christ might be given to them that believe.*

And if we believe?

.*.ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus.*
*For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ.*
*There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus. And if ye be Christ's, then are ye Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise.*

teachings.title: The mystery: Gentiles are fellowheirs
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: The mystery revealed to Paul is that Gentiles are fellowheirs in Christ, under the same dispensation of grace given to all men since Adam, not a separate one.
teachings.text:
For the cause of the good news, that all who believe are joint heirs, in Christ, Paul is writing as a prisoner. In chains, under tribulation, but free in Christ, he wants the Gentiles reading this epistle to understand the depths of his devotion towards the ministry unto them that he has received from God. A dispensation of grace given unto the Gentiles as it already had been to the Jews, in faith through Christ.

What had in times past been a mystery. How God would achieve the promise of all nations being blessed in Abraham's seed, Jesus. Now Paul understands the mystery and is explaining it to them.

That the Gentiles should be fellowheirs, and of the same body and partakers of His promise, in Christ by the Gospel.

Paul's mission is to reveal the answer to this mystery, to proclaim the good news. To make all men see.

This dispensation of grace is being extended to all, is not a different dispensation as some would claim, but the same as given the Israelites, and all men, from Adam. Since Seth and his sons called upon the name of the Lord. All who bow their knees unto the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, of whom the whole family in heaven and earth is named.

We are a holy and separate people, called by His name.

And as such, with Christ dwelling in our hearts by faith, we are able to know the breadth, length, depth, and height of all the bounty of blessings made available to God's children. Amen.

teachings.title: To thy seed, which is Christ
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: The promises to Abraham's seed are fulfilled in Christ, in whom believers inherit the land forever, while Lot pitching his tent toward Sodom warns against choosing worldly ease.
teachings.text:
Chapter 13 of Genesis brings Abram and Sarai and his nephew Lot back to the land of Canaan, back to where Abram called upon the name of the Lord, near Bethel, which is on the West bank of the Jordan, in the area of Jerusalem and Bethlehem. There, scripture reminds us, he had built an altar.

Because of the greatness of his herds and Lot's, and growing contentions between each other's herdsmen, he gives Lot a choice of grazing land, and Lot chooses the area around the plains of the Jordan, just above what's called the Dead Sea today.

Given the choice, and seeing there was much water and vegetation, *even as the garden of the Lord, like the land of Egypt.* And so enticed, he pitches his tent there to the east, towards Sodom. There's many times in life we are given a choice like this, and choosing from ease or greed or comfort, we pitch our tents towards Sodom, towards wickedness and sin. There's a spiritual application there.

Abram, meanwhile, settles down to Hebron and the plains of Mamre. And God gives Abram two more promises, *all the land which thou seest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed for ever,* and *I will make thy seed as the dust of the earth,* too numerous to count.

The Bible says in **Galatians 3:16**

*Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ.*

Christ is the answer to the promises, kept by God. Jesus is the seed through whom all nations are blessed. It is in Jesus that the promised land is given forever, to those who believe and call upon the name of the Lord. It is in this seed that Abram can be said to have fathered a people too numerous to count, saved sons of God.

*Then Abram removed his tent, and came and dwelt in the plain of Mamre, which is in Hebron, and built there an altar unto the* Lord*.*

teachings.title: Thy seed as the stars: one promise, one faith
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: The promise of seed as the stars is fulfilled in Christ and the innumerable redeemed of Revelation 7, not the modern Jew, under one faith in both testaments.
teachings.text:
The word of God came to Abram in a vision.

**John 1:1-2**
*In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. The same was in the beginning with God*.

The Bible tells us who the word of God is. It is Jesus.

*Fear not, Abram: I am thy shield, and thy exceeding great reward.*

Abram, old when he called upon the name of the Lord and received blessings and promises, now even older and without a true heir, questions the Lord. *Behold, to me thou hast given no seed: and, lo, one born in my house is mine heir.* Abram's faith tested, the word of God says to him: *This shall not be thine heir; but he that shall come forth out of thine own bowels shall be thine heir. And he brought him forth abroad, and said, Look now toward heaven, and tell the stars, if thou be able to number them: and he said unto him, So shall thy seed be.*

We see in scripture that this promise was kept, his seed being one, Jesus Christ. And in Him the promise of a nation innumerable, like the stars in the sky, is fufifiled in **Revelation 7**. That following the tribulation and the rapture, there are saints, redeemed in the blood of Christ. 144,000 Old Testament saints, 12,000 from each of the tribes listed (not Jews, but Israelites) and; *A great multitude, which no man could number, of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues.*

This is the promise to Abraham. Not for the modern Jew. Not for the apostate and wicked modern state calling itself Israel. But of Christ and Him crucified, with the power to make the elect heirs to the Kingdom of Heaven; whosoever will call upon the name of the Lord.

Old Testament. New Testament. The same dispensation. The same promise. The same faith.

teachings.title: Circumcision of the heart
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Abraham's circumcision pictured the circumcision of the heart by the Spirit, for a true Jew is one inwardly.
teachings.text:
Now, Abram becomes Abraham, decades after his salvation by calling upon the name of the Lord, and is given the physical sign of the covenant, circumcision of the flesh.

Of course, this physical act of obedience was a picture of the sealing a soul by the Holy Spirit to come. The circumcision of the heart.

**Romans 2**
*28 For he is not a Jew, which is one outwardly; neither is that circumcision, which is outward in the flesh:*

*29 But he is a Jew, which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter; whose praise is not of men, but of God*

**Colossians 2:11**
*In whom also ye are circumcised with the circumcision made without hands, in putting off the body of the sins of the flesh by the circumcision of Christ:*

For while the descendants of Abraham kept the circumcision as an ordinance to remember their covenant with God that brought about Christ Jesus in the flesh, to preserve the seed, even as strangers and bondsmen were added to the nation, in case any forgot God's promise, the circumcision of the heart which is found in believers is to us who are saved a reminder of our salvation and belonging to the body of Christ.

teachings.title: If ye be Christ's, then are ye Abraham's seed
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Abraham's blessing passed to Isaac and is fulfilled in Christ, so all believers are Abraham's seed and heirs according to the promise.
teachings.text:
Abraham was 175 when he died. He was 137 when Sarah died, and here it says he remarried and had at least 6 sons with Keturah, and they begat many sons, but the physical inheritance and the spiritual blessing, given Abraham by God concerning Jesus, Abraham passes down to Isaac. The child of faith.

*And Abraham gave all that he had to Isaac.*

*Then Abraham gave up the ghost, and died in a good old age, an old man, and full of years; and was gathered to his people.*

*And his sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron the son of Zohar the Hittite, which is before Mamre; The field which Abraham purchased of the sons of Heth: there was Abraham buried, and Sarah his wife.*

Abraham died and was gathered to his people, in heaven. It couldn't be into his own "bosom" after all. But the patriarch is given an end of days and an account of his death, which the Bible uses to signify the humanity of the fathers and the prophets.

Christ Jesus comments on the faith of Abraham and his joy at the fulfillment of the promise made to him in **John 8**;

 *Your father Abraham rejoiced to see my day: and he saw it, and was glad.*..*Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was, I am.*

And so it was that Abraham's seed was a blessing to the whole world, especially of those who believe.

**Galatians 3**

*For ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus. For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ.*

*There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus. And if ye be Christ's, then are ye Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise.*

Let this comfort you who believe, and drive to envy those of you still on the fence, trusting your own righteousness to provide your own salvation, bringing you to repent. Knowing Abraham trusted God and obtained the righteousness of Christ, and so to do we. For God is not slack concerning His promises. And we who are of Abraham's seed in Christ Jesus are joint heirs with Him. Rejoice!

teachings.title: Jews Falsely So-Called Are Spiritually Edom
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: There is no ethnic role in salvation, so the Jews who reject Christ are spiritually Edom while believers are spiritually Israel heirs of a better country.
teachings.text:
In the end, we are told by history, when there was a rebellion against Rome in 70AD, it included the ethnic line of Judah. The remnants of Benjamin and Levi. And whatever Edomites who remained. All constituted what became known collectively as Jews. And, according to the history, all were wiped out and scattered abroad, forbidden by Rome to return to Judea.

Much speculation has risen out of these events and about these people. It is a rabbi hole that can be fascinating to go down, but what matters really is what God's word clearly says.

We can't know anything else for certain, as it becomes arguing genealogies and Jewish fables.

What I believe is that, because there is no genetic or ethnic role in salvation, that it is individual souls that are saved, that flesh profiteth nothing, that to here is neither Jew nor Greek, pursuit of the racial lines of Edom and Jews, the tribes of Israelites, etc, should really only be looked at in a carnal, earthly way. A fun pass time. Something to wonder about in our idleness. Spiritually, whatever happened to them is irrelevant.

We know Jews, falsely so-called, Synagogue of Satan, those who say they are Jews but are not, are spiritually Edom. Regardless of what Kaiser Sose origin story they muddy the waters with.

They were taken out of the physical promised land for rejection of Christ. Whatever claim they had to the promise ended with the fulfilment of the blessing, which is in Jesus.

And if the Jews who are spiritually Edom, who sold their birthright and blessing for earthly things, are actual sons of Esau, who is Edom, seeking to steal back the birthright Jacob took, it doesn't change anything for us who are spiritually Israel.

We know they are antichrists. We know the Gospel is the truth. We look forward to a better country, a kingdom we are inheritors of through God's grace and mercy, in Christ. Let them squabble over dessert sand. Let them persecute us in Jesus's name. We have already overcome.

teachings.title: The Key of David Opens and Shuts
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Christ opens the door of salvation that none can shut and also shuts in reprobation, and those who say they are Jews but deny Christ are liars, spiritually Edom.
teachings.text:
*And to the angel of the church in Philadelphia write; These things saith he that is holy, he that is true, he that hath the key of David, he that openeth, and no man shutteth; and shutteth, and no man openeth;*

Jesus addresses the church at Philadelphia. Jesus is holy and true. He has the key of David, mentioned in **Isaiah 22:22**:

*And the key of the house of David will I lay upon his shoulder; so he shall open, and none shall shut; and he shall shut, and none shall open.*

To Him gave all the prophets witness.

Also, don't miss this, Jesus opens the door of salvation to us as individual believers, and none may shut it. We have eternal life. It can't be lost or taken. But Christ Jesus also has the ability to shut the door, that none may open. This is reprobation, and it's a doctrine found throughout the Bible. Many find it difficult to accept or believe, but it is taught throughout scripture, clearly and with examples. Sadly today, many are offended at the concept.

Jesus continues, praising them for their faith. Promising He's opened the door for them. Man has little strength. We cannot open that door ourselves, only His may.

*I know thy works: behold, I have set before thee an open door, and no man can shut it: for thou hast a little strength, and hast kept my word, and hast not denied my name. Behold, I will make them of the synagogue of Satan, which say they are Jews, and are not, but do lie; behold, I will make them to come and worship before thy feet, and to know that I have loved thee.*

The church in Philadelphia is being persecuted, like some of the others, and again it is the Jews. Jesus says they say they are Jews but are not. That they are liars.

There are theories and interpretations as to what this means. Edomites? The Ashkenazi? Khazarians? These are earthly interpretations, with physical/genetic/ethnic implications. And they may very well be a marker that has some application. But what we know for certain, spiritually, that they who say they are Jews but are not, are spiritually Edom indeed. They are Esau, who sold their birthright, which has been taken by the Gentiles who are spiritually Jacob.

**Romans 2:28-29**
*For he is not a Jew, which is one outwardly; neither is that circumcision, which is outward in the flesh: But he is a Jew, which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter; whose praise is not of men, but of God.*

For us, it is sufficient to understand that those who reject the Son have not the Father. That those who deny Jesus is the Christ are liars, and antichrists. By focusing on the spiritual application, it becomes inarguable that they who say they are Jews are not, but are liars. Without going down rabbi holes arguing about their origins and debates about genealogies. The word of God is sharper than any arguments of man, and discerns quickly exactly why they are not Jews; for if they kept the law of Moses and believed the prophets, they would believe Jesus is who He says He is. That He is the Christ.

But we who are spiritually His, who are inwardly circumcised of the heart, we can take solace in our tribulations caused by the wicked Jew antichrists, that they are a synagogue of Satan and Jesus will make them worship at His feet and know that He loves us, His brothers and sisters who believed on His name. Who trusted God's word.

Every knee shall bow and every tongue confess. Amen!

Continuing to the Philadelphians;
*Because thou hast kept the word of my patience, I also will keep thee from the hour of temptation, which shall come upon all the world, to try them that dwell upon the earth. Behold, I come quickly: hold that fast which thou hast, that no man take thy crown.*

Jesus encourages them. They are doing well. Holdfast. Faint not. And as the temptation, the test of the deceiver, comes upon the world, they who remain patient and true will be protected from the deception. Note that Jesus encourages them to maintain their works and faith that they not lose crowns. Crowns are rewards in Heaven given to believers based on our works.

teachings.title: The vineyard given to others
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: In the parable of the husbandmen God takes the vineyard of His covenant from the unfruitful Jewish leaders and gives it to others, the replacement theology found throughout the Bible.
teachings.text:
It's important to point out and interesting to consider that the same authority who ordained John's baptism, Who sent the prophets and beloved Son, Is the same authority who put these husbandmen in charge. God the Father. Jehovah LORD.

And the vineyard, being His covenant, and the fruit thereof His people, Jesus telling them that they are rebellious to the authority that they question of Christ, that they will have the vineyard, the care of that covenant, taken from them and given to others.

To which they react, "God forbid!"

This is what is called today. Replacement Theology. This idea that the vineyard has been given to others, to be overseen by other people, Who aren't the Jews. Who aren't the Levitical priesthood. Who aren't the scribes and lawyers and Pharisees and Sadducees, the elders who were unfruitful. The rebellious husbandmen, these unfruitful vine are cut off and burned.

The covenant given to another people. A New Testament.

The idea of replacement theology is found throughout the Bible. It is not some newfound doctrine, it isn't some Paulian heresy. It is the will of God the Father.

It is just. It is righteous. It has happened.

And all those who deny it, who defend these rebellious husbandmen, let them be accursed for rejecting the judgment of God and defending the murderers of Christ Jesus.

teachings.title: If ye will obey, a peculiar treasure
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: The Sinai covenant was conditional and Israel broke it, so it was replaced by the new covenant and those saved in Christ are now God's peculiar people, refuting dispensational Zionism.
teachings.text:
IF *ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people: for all the earth is mine.*

This is the foundation of the covenant at Sinai, the promise made to the children of Israel by God, that IF they kept it, they would be a peculiar people, special to God.

God judges nations on earth by their works. He judges people as individuals by their faith. His promises to nations are conditional. They are if/then. To us as individual souls, the only condition to be His is faith in Christ.

The if/then covenant with Israel, that they broke themselves repeatedly, despite God's longsuffering and mercy, despite being given chance after chance to get right, they broke entirely with the Crucifixion, the rejection of Hia Son Jesus. But it is in Jesus that are made partakers of the new and better covenant. The better testament. And the old one is done away with.

*For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second.*

And where was the fault of the first? In the Israelites.

*For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord. For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord; I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people: And they shall not teach every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the Lord: for all shall know me, from the least to the greatest. For I will be merciful to their unrighteousness, and their sins and their iniquities will I remember no more. In that he saith, A new covenant, he hath made the first old. Now that which decayeth and waxeth old is ready to vanish away.*

This is the bookend to the Saini covenant, fulfilled:
*I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord.*

And this should be the final nail in the coffin for the Dispensationalist Zionist heresy that God is still on the hook for the first covenant. No, He has replaced the physical nation with a new one. Israel was to be a peculiar people, but failed. Now His peculiar people are those saved in Christ.

*But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light; Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God: which had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy.*

teachings.title: The entire Bible teaches one faith in Christ
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: What is mocked as replacement theology is simply the Bible's one theme of salvation in Christ from Moses to Revelation, which dispensationalism denies.
teachings.text:
The entire Bible teaches what is derisively called replacement theology. Better phrased; The entire Bible teaches the one faith of salvation and redemption in Christ. The failure of man in the flesh to find holiness in the works of their own righteousness, and the grace and mercy of God in providing a sacrifice for their sin that they may know Him. For God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son that whosoever believeth on Him shall not perish but have everlasting life.

Moses wrote of Jesus, in Genesis. In Exodus. In Leviticus and Deuteronomy. The prophets spoke of Him, and preached His gospel of redemption and reconciliation. The Psalms sing of Him and His coming. Jesus Christ in the flesh spent 3.5 years of an earthly ministry reaching the lost sheep of Israel that He could lead who were His, calling them to repentance and preaching to the unbelieving that they were going to be replaced and cast into outer darkness with wailing and gnashing of teeth.

Once the veil is torn at the death of Christ, the remaining scripture teaches of the gospel given to a people who were not a nation, now heirs to the Kingdom. The branches that did not produce fruit meet for repentance, cast into the fire.

The epistles giving us the grafting in, the theology of salvation and religion undefiled. The Revelation of Christ Jesus, the rapture of believers, the resurrection, adoption and redemption God predestined in His Son. And God's final judgement that we may know it, and come to Him before it's too late.

And it is this simple truth, the entire theme of scripture, that the false doctrine of dispensationalism denies and rejects.

teachings.title: The children of the flesh are not the children of God
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Romans 9 shows Israel after the flesh is cut off and the election is of the seed, Christ, not individual Calvinist election, and God has mercy on whom He will.
teachings.text:
Having established all things regarding salvation by faith, and the implications to man: believers unto righteousness found in Christ Jesus, the new man, the Spirit, and the promise of the incorruptible that comes at the redemption (as well as the sin of the flesh in the meantime), unbelief unto death, and reprobates, twice-dead, hearts hardened, Paul now moves on to addressing the Jews after the flesh, considering these settled arguments from before.

If all these things are true, and the gospel is by faith in Christ, which the prophets who came before all testified, and the law was unto death (not because of the unrighteousness of the law, but rather the infirmities of the people), and if all are under sin, Jew or Gentile, and all require faith in Christ to be saved, for there is no difference, what then?

Paul begins by expressing his sorrow that his kinsmen, the unbelieving children of Israel after the flesh are cut off. That they have had the Kingdom taken from them, as Jesus said.

*Israelites; to whom pertaineth the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the service of God, and the promises; Whose are the fathers, and of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came, who is over all, God blessed for ever. Amen.*

All of these blessings, and the seed pertaining to the promise that is Christ Jesus (concerning the flesh, note the distinction, especially those "mother of God" heretics), and yet Israel are cut off.

*They which are the children of the flesh, these are not the children of God*.

(Dispensationalists should read that again and again until it sinks in)

...*but the children of the promise are counted for the seed. For this is the word of promise, At this time will I come, and Sarah shall have a son. And not only this; but when Rebecca also had conceived by one, even by our father Isaac*.

The promise was of the seed, the seed being Christ in the flesh, who came of the line of Jacob, born second but given the inheritance and the blessing over Esau.

**Malachi 1:2-3**
*I have loved you, saith the Lord. Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us? Was not Esau Jacob's brother? saith the Lord: yet I loved Jacob, And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.*

This is pertaining to the seed, the promise of Christ, knowing Edom would be made desolate, the election is of Jacob/Israel, that Jesus would come from Judah, the root of Jesse, from the throne of David.

This is not about individual salvation of Esau or Jacob. The election of the seed is in Christ. And it served God that the older served the younger in the promise,  in the same way that the Jew made way for the Gentile.

But the law says the older shall have the inheritance , so what then, is God unrighteous?

*God forbid. For he saith to Moses, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion.*

We trust the judgment of God. Who knows beginning from end. That all are chosen in Christ, not unto belief. Not given faith by God, but predestined in Christ to be given the blessing, the promise and the inheritance, to all who believe.

And so God, in His wisdom, shows mercy to who He will show mercy. And compassion on whom He will.

And harden the hearts of those fitted for destruction. All to His glory. Because as we have established; the righteousness of God is revealed both in His mercy towards us, and the love that gave His only begotten Son for us, but in His wrath against those who hold the truth in unrighteousness.

teachings.title: All Israel saved in Christ
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Unbelieving Jews were made reprobate like Pharaoh while a believing remnant remains, since all God's promises are kept in Christ the one seed.
teachings.text:
And so, as Paul in the Spirit testifies, he wishes that his brothers after the flesh would come to the faith. But they are cut off. Just as Esau become Edom, and they were made desolate, Jews were cut off and consumed.

Is God's judgment unrighteous? No. Is His word unfaithful? Again no, for a remnant remains, those saved by faith as is Paul, and to believing Jews whom he writes to in Rome. But the unbelieving Jew, hearts hardened, had their chance, and their destruction served to show the glory of God.

*For the scripture saith unto Pharaoh, Even for this same purpose have I raised thee up, that I might shew my power in thee, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth.*

Just as Pharaoh was made reprobate, so too are the Jews after the flesh.

God's promises were kept in Christ. The remnant is in Christ. All Israel was saved, in Christ. The Kingdom, the land that was promised, is through Christ. The blessings were to the seed, and that seed is singular; Christ.

teachings.title: A remnant according to the election of grace
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Romans 11 does not make unbelieving Jews God's chosen; only a remnant elected by grace through faith is saved while the rest are blinded.
teachings.text:
And so, Paul having settled the matter regarding Israel after the flesh, that none are saved without faith in Christ, same as the Gentiles, dead under sin just as the Gentiles are, that any zeal they show towards God, without faith, is out of ignorance and going about to establish their own righteousness, all together vain; He continues stating his fervent desire that his brothers after the flesh repent, and be saved.

This chapter is abused into teaching a false doctrine that all Jews, even the modern "Jews" (who say they are Jews but do lie), are still God's chosen people and thus still are going to be saved, despite being apostate and denying Christ Jesus. They will derisively dismiss the idea that non-believing Jews are cut off and cast out, ears dulled and hearts waxen, unable to believe, as "Replacement Theology."

But the epistle to the Romans demonstrates with finality that all who don't believe are cut off, and that it is one continuation of faith that saves. The same for Jew and Greek. It isn't replacement it is continual, in the election of grace.

Old Testament Israel and New Testament Israel. Hebrew of Gentiles, all were saved by faith. The offer to the Greek came after Christ was lifted up, but it is the same offer. The same gift of eternal life in Christ through faith. Being chosen to be God's people by our belief, not by seed. Wild olive branches grafted in to the root that is found in Israel, as unbelieving Jews are cut off and burned.

Paul begins the chapter giving a rhetorical question to the conclusions he reached regarding apostate Jews in the previous chapters. *Hath God cast away his people? God forbid.* Why? Because he himself is of the Jews and a believer. So were most of the early churches. The remnant of those elect in grace, predestined in Christ (not as Calvanism teaches, but by our faith through Christ, not the other way around). If he, Paul is saved then not all of Israel is cast away. God hath not cast away his people who he foreknew. Again, those that are saved and in whom He works to make vessels fitted to His use. It is the same foreknowledge of the elect, those that would believe, not saying every Jew.

The prophet Elijah cursing Israel for their unbelief, saying "Lord, they have killed thy prophets, and digged down thine altars; and I am left alone, and they seek my life," is reminded by God that He has a remnant of believers still. As wicked and apostate as Israel got, there were still 7,000 who had not bowed the knee to Baal. Paul using this to say that even then, there were Jews who believed and got saved. That all of them were not cast out.

*Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace.*

The remnant is according to what? The election of grace. Which is as he already established, being saved by faith calling upon the name of the Lord. This is a conditional statement. Dispensationalism always ignores conditional statements regarding the Jews to make these things apply to all of them.

And, as an aside he makes yet another statement of salvation by faith and not of works;
*And if by grace, then is it no more of works: otherwise grace is no more grace. But if it be of works, then it is no more grace: otherwise work is no more work*.

There is no grace if you worked for it. There is no working for it if it is of grace.

What then? If only a remnant remains of those who believed, then Israel as a nation has not obtained righteousness (they seek to establish their own), but the election in grace, believers, have obtained righteousness by faith.

And the rest were blinded. Which brings us back to chapter 1 and the reprobate doctrine. God chooses to blind those who will not believe, giving them up and giving them over.

*According as it is written, God hath given them the spirit of slumber, eyes that they should not see, and ears that they should not hear*.

As Jesus said in **Matthew 13**, eyes closed, dull of hearing, hearts waxed gross, they cannot hear the word of God and believe.

teachings.title: Boast not against the branches
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: The Gentiles are grafted into the root by grace, so they must not boast but fear, since God who cut off the natural branches could cut them off too.
teachings.text:
Continuing the thought, Paul uses a parable, a picture of what has happened, that the natural root of salvation came through Israel, and though some of those branches were broken off and burned, the Gentiles were grafted in. All by grace through faith.

And Paul warns the Gentiles not to think too highly of themselves, that it is by God's grace and to His purpose that this has happened.

We aren't naturally supposed to be there, being wild olive trees, and the tree of the vineyard that God has grown with care is pruned of the branches that aren't producing fruit, and grafted us in that will produce in an abundance, but again the glory is His.

*Boast not against the branches. But if thou boast, thou bearest not the root, but the root thee.*

We shouldn't fall to the same arrogance as the unbelieving Jews. To think we are special boys. There is no Jew or Greek in Christ. Keep humility about our situation. We all deserve Hell and Death. We are there simply by the grace and the purpose of God.

*Thou wilt say then, The branches were broken off, that I might be grafted in.*
*Well; because of unbelief they were broken off, and thou standest by faith. Be not highminded, but fear: For if God spared not the natural branches, take heed lest he also spare not thee.*

Well there means , good. Correct. You are right. The Jews were cut off that we may be grafted in. So true.

But be not high-minded, or proud, because of God did that to the nation he tended for thousands of years, He could easily do that to the Gentiles. The other nations.

teachings.title: Until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Being grafted in is conditional on faith, and the fulness of the Gentiles simply means the harvest, when the Lord reaps at His coming before the wrath.
teachings.text:
*Behold therefore the goodness and severity of God: on them which fell, severity; but toward thee, goodness, if thou continue in his goodness: otherwise thou also shalt be cut off. And they also, if they abide not still in unbelief, shall be grafted in: for God is able to graft them in again*.

Again, note the conditional statements. IF we as a people continue in belief, we will remain in His goodness, and IF the Jew in unbelief repents, they will be graft back in. It is entirely conditioned on faith.

*For I would not, brethren, that ye should be ignorant of this mystery, lest ye should be wise in your own conceits; that blindness in part is happened to Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in.*

So many miss the point of this statement, which is a warning to the nations not to assume they deserve the blessings of grace through faith, as the unregenerate Jew had done. They get caught up in the "fullness of the Gentiles come in."

It is a curious turn of phrase that, because it points to a future event, many take and wrest with, trying to pinpoint what this means eschatologically. But it simply means when all those that are going to believe, have, the harvest comes. The day of the Lord, the rapture and the wrath. It's just a poetic way of saying this. Fullness being synonymous with the harvest. The fruit coming in. It isn't some esoteric hidden meaning.

Paul says that blindness *in part* (there's a remnant that believed, remember) has happened until the harvest of the nations is ready.

**Revelation 14:15**
*And another angel came out of the temple, crying with a loud voice to him that sat on the cloud, Thrust in thy sickle, and reap: for the time is come for thee to reap; for the harvest of the earth is ripe.*

God likens all of this to a vineyard throughout scripture. The spring feasts and fall feasts point to the first and second coming, the sowing and the harvest.

The fruits we produce are saved Christians we've led to Christ. The increase, the bounty of the harvest is God's. We are servants, husbandmen. He is the Lord of the harvest. And when the fullness of the Gentiles has come in, He will reap.

teachings.title: The covenant kept in Christ, not in the Jews
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Leviticus 26's remedy of confession is fulfilled in Christ, and God's Israel is believers circumcised in heart, while unbelieving Jews remain under the curse.
teachings.text:
**Leviticus 26** is one of the many times God reiterates the warning to Israel, that if they don't keep the conditions of the covenant God has made with them, he will curse them 7-fold, remove them from the land and set their enemies up over them.

This held specific meaning to the Hebrews in the wilderness, entering into Canaan, but it is true of all people who call themselves by His name.

**2 Chronicles 7:14**
*If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.*

The curse against His people comes with a remedy. Because the Lord is a forgiving and merciful God.

*If they shall confess their iniquity, and the iniquity of their fathers, with their trespass which they trespassed against me, and that also they have walked contrary unto me; And that I also have walked contrary unto them, and have brought them into the land of their enemies; if then their uncircumcised hearts be humbled, and they then accept of the punishment of their iniquity: Then will I remember my covenant with Jacob, and also my covenant with Isaac, and also my covenant with Abraham will I remember; and I will remember the land.*

(Note the physical circumcision availa them nothing. It is the circumcision of the heart, made without hands, in Christ Jesus;

*In whom also ye are circumcised with the circumcision made without hands, in putting off the body of the sins of the flesh by the circumcision of Christ*.
...
*But he is a Jew, which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter; whose praise is not of men, but of God.*)

This covenant is and always has been kept in Christ. It was to Abraham's seed, who is Jesus, and those blessings fall on those adopted into the promise by faith in Him. Those calling themselves Jews today *could* repent to be partakers of the promise, but note that they'd have to admit not only that they forsook God and didn't walk in His statutes, rejecting Christ, and deserved their punishments, but they'd have to also testify that God has walked contrary to them, and that His judgment was right.

In the various captivites and tribulations of the OT Israelites, this repentance led to their being restored. But modern Jews, so-called, maintain in their being scattered, in their being cursed, in their being kept from peace in the land, they keep the fiction that they remain God's chosen people. That they aren't being cursed for their unbelief, but that it is we who believe, those circumcised of the heart, who afflict them unjustly.

*And upon them that are left alive of you I will send a faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies; and the sound of a shaken leaf shall chase them; and they shall flee, as fleeing from a sword; and they shall fall when none pursueth.*

This is seen in the ADL and the cries of "antisemetism," seeing swastikas and threats of genocide in construction markings and preaching from the Bible. The wicked flee where none pursue. They are faint of heart, as the Lord promises.

Talmudic rabbinical Judasism shows that they despise God's statutes and abhor His judgements, so that they do not keep His commandments but instead find loopholes and rationalizations in the vain traditions of men, doctrines they invented taught as commandments of God.

His tabernacle is not set in their midst, who is Jesus. They are contrary to all men. God's wrath abides upon them to the uttermost.

God's people, Israel, has always been a nation of believers who, by faith, carry the circumcision of the heart. Today it is believing Christians, and our nations are blessed by the few within it who keep the word of God, and cursed when we who call ourselves by His name reject His judgement.

teachings.title: Circumcise your hearts, O Jerusalem
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: God called Judah to repent with a circumcision of the heart by faith rather than of the flesh, but they were a stiff-necked people whose destruction was their own doing.
teachings.text:
Chapter 4, and the Spirit of the Lord is upon Jeremiah, preaching to the people of Judah, the children of Israel, and warning them of destruction coming from the North, the lion of Babylon. God giving the prophet visions of an invasion, all the whole the supposed prophets of the Lord are preaching "peace, peace." (As we will see in a later chapter, they are falsely telling Judah that they are fine and God loves them, but they aren't speaking for God).

The Lord tells the people to repent towards Him and He will stay His judgment. To the circumcision of the heart. Not of the flesh, the outward sign of being of the seed of Abraham, but the circumcision made without hands, of faith in the Lord.

**Romans 2:25-29**
*For circumcision verily profiteth, if thou keep the law: but if thou be a breaker of the law, thy circumcision is made uncircumcision. Therefore if the uncircumcision keep the righteousness of the law, shall not his uncircumcision be counted for circumcision? And shall not uncircumcision which is by nature, if it fulfil the law, judge thee, who by the letter and circumcision dost transgress the law? For he is not a Jew, which is one outwardly; neither is that circumcision, which is outward in the flesh: But he is a Jew, which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter; whose praise is not of men, but of God.*

**Colossians 2:11**
 *In whom also ye are circumcised with the circumcision made without hands, in putting off the body of the sins of the flesh by the circumcision of Christ:*

Even as God is warning of utter destruction and the desolation of her cities, being spoiled by these invading armies, carried away into captivity, justified in His wrath, God offers His grace that if they but turn back to Him, He will repent.

*O Jerusalem, wash thine heart from wickedness, that thou mayest be saved. How long shall thy vain thoughts lodge within thee?*

We can hear in this the frustration and pleading of the Lord, longsuffering and merciful, at the end of His patience. Sorrowful and lamenting what He will do because they are a stiff-necked and gainsaying people. The same frustration Jesus felt, preaching to the Jews, 600yrs later.

**Matthew 23:37**
*O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!*

God says the punishment coming is due to their own wickedness, their bitter heart. Wise to do evil, but to do good they have no knowledge. Their destruction is their own doing, and God laments this, as a husband would putting away his wife that he loves for her adultery.

Jeremiah sees visions of desolation, cities sacked and spoiled. The sky black from smoke. The fields, destroyed. Even the birds fleeing, for there are no men left.

And the Lord, who is a jealous God, asks what will Israel do when its destruction has come? He compares the nation to an old harlot. Decked in crimson, face caked with makeup, appealing to her lovers that she fornicated with, the other nations and their gods, and He says without Him. Without their land and riches. These lovers will turn and seek their lives. Without God they are vanity.

teachings.title: Continuation theology, not replacement theology
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Israel's broken branches and the grafting in of believers show one promise by grace through faith in the same Christ, which is why the cut-off hate us.
teachings.text:
**John 15:1-8**
 *I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman. Every branch in me that beareth not fruit he taketh away: and every branch that beareth fruit, he purgeth it, that it may bring forth more fruit. Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you. Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; no more can ye, except ye abide in me. I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing. If a man abide not in me, he is cast forth as a branch, and is withered; and men gather them, and cast them into the fire, and they are burned. If ye abide in me, and my words abide in you, ye shall ask what ye will, and it shall be done unto you. Herein is my Father glorified, that ye bear much fruit; so shall ye be my disciples.*

**Romans 11:17-25**
*And if some of the branches be broken off, and thou, being a wild olive tree, wert grafted in among them, and with them partakest of the root and fatness of the olive tree; Boast not against the branches. But if thou boast, thou bearest not the root, but the root thee. Thou wilt say then, The branches were broken off, that I might be grafted in. Well; because of unbelief they were broken off, and thou standest by faith. Be not highminded, but fear: For if God spared not the natural branches, take heed lest he also spare not thee. Behold therefore the goodness and severity of God: on them which fell, severity; but toward thee, goodness, if thou continue in his goodness: otherwise thou also shalt be cut off. And they also, if they abide not still in unbelief, shall be grafted in: for God is able to graft them in again. For if thou wert cut out of the olive tree which is wild by nature, and wert grafted contrary to nature into a good olive tree: how much more shall these, which be the natural branches, be grafted into their own olive tree? For I would not, brethren, that ye should be ignorant of this mystery, lest ye should be wise in your own conceits; that blindness in part is happened to Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in.*

Jeremiah preaching to the Jews says; *The Lord called thy name, A green olive tree, fair, and of goodly fruit: with the noise of a great tumult he hath kindled fire upon it, and the branches of it are broken.* A theme repeatedly used in scripture. And for the nation of Judah, this preaching produced the same reaction against him as it had against Jesus and the Apostles. The same reaction we get today as spiritual Israel, when we remind those who say they are Jews but are not but do lie, that we have been graft into the vine that is Christ. But they have been cut off to be burned: They threaten Jeremiah's life.

*And the Lord hath given me knowledge of it, and I know it: then thou shewedst me their doings. But I was like a lamb or an ox that is brought to the slaughter; and I knew not that they had devised devices against me, saying, Let us destroy the tree with the fruit thereof, and let us cut him off from the land of the living, that his name may be no more remembered. But, O Lord of hosts, that judgest righteously, that triest the reins and the heart, let me see thy vengeance on them: for unto thee have I revealed my cause. Therefore thus saith the Lord of the men of Anathoth, that seek thy life, saying, Prophesy not in the name of the Lord, that thou die not by our hand*

They call it "replacement theology," but it is actually a continuation theology, the same promise offered by the same grace, through faith in the same Christ, the Lord Jesus.

And for this truth, they seek to kill us. Because they hated Christ first.

teachings.title: The righteous remnant and replacement theology
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: So-called replacement theology is God's will to show mercy on vessels prepared unto glory, always preserving a remnant saved by faith rather than works.
teachings.text:
Of course one of the applications we can take from this all, is that the idea of "replacement theology," really is simply understanding God's will. That He hath mercy on whom He will have mercy, and whom He will He hardeneth, *that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, which he had afore prepared unto glory*.

But there is always a righteous remnant. Those 7000 who have not bent the knee to Baal. And in who God will that His glory and mercy be seen that others may believe.

**Isaiah 1:9**
*Except the LORD of hosts had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, and we should have been like unto Gomorrah.*

And it is that faith that comes from seeing His wrath on those fitted for destruction, the clay marred and discarded by the potter, and the glory of the vessels fitted for His purpose, that reveals the truth to the unbelieving that they may come to be saved by faith. Not by their own works, which is the path that led to the destruction of the Jew;

*What shall we say then? That the Gentiles, which followed not after righteousness, have attained to righteousness, even the righteousness which is of faith. But Israel, which followed after the law of righteousness, hath not attained to the law of righteousness. Wherefore? Because they sought it not by faith, but as it were by the works of the law. For they stumbled at that stumblingstone; As it is written, Behold, I lay in Sion a stumblingstone and rock of offence: and whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed.*

teachings.title: Jeremiah's field: a pledge of redemption
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Jeremiah's purchase of a field during the siege promised Judah's return and, in dual fulfilment, the everlasting covenant with the Israel of God saved by faith.
teachings.text:
And so, here in **Jeremiah 32** we find the prophet held in a prison in King Zedekiah's home, as Jerusalem is besieged by the Chaldeans of Babylon. And the king is frustrated with the prophesying of spoil and desolation coming from the word of God through Jeremiah. The prediction of Judah being led to captivity, slain by sword and pestilence has left the king and those in the court in despair.

And then, the word of the Lord comes to Jeremiah the Benjaminite, and tells him of a real estate deal in the midst of a terrible siege.

It seems an unlikely thing, but the Lord instructs Jeremiah to take up the offer made to him by Hanameel, son of Shallum, the prophets uncle. A family member of the same tribe, who wishes to sell him a field in their lands, under the right of redemption. The return of lands to the people of the tribes during Jubilee.

God tells him it will happen, and it does. And he conducts the transaction according to law, witnessed and subscribed, the paperwork done. The evidences of purchase, God says to place in an earthen vessel for preservation, because this is the Lord's promise; that there will be a return. That all is not lost. A day of redemption will come and His people will have their portion of the land of milk and honey again.

And the word of the Lord tells the curse that's upon Judah, and the wickedness of the people, and the certain destruction that's upon them for their iniquities and abominations. The idols and incense burned in the house of the Lord. The high places built to Moloch, where the children of Judah pass their own children through the fire in sacrifice, something so wicked, God hadn't imagined it would be. (Men invent evil in their hearts, not commanded by God who is without sin and holy)

And having said all this, and promising the triumph of Nebuchadnezzar over them, God tells them through the prophet of His mercy. That they who are scattered and are His people will be returned again. Both the captivity, at the end of the 70 years, but in a larger sense the Israel of God. The saved and scattered nations, who shall have redemption in the land. Who shall be His people and He shall be our God.

Given one heart and one way, saved by the gospel, that we may fear Him forever, sealed by the Spirit. An everlasting covenant where God will never turn from us, the love and respect for Him, fear of the Lord, kept in our hearts that we shall not depart from Him.

In the dual fulfilment of this prophecy, God uses the transaction of the field to give hope to those with an ear to hear. That their captivity won't be forever. That men shall buy fields in the land of their fathers again, for He will cause their captivity to return. But in it, He shows us His promise to all those who are saved by faith on His word.

teachings.title: A remnant according to the election of grace
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: God saves or condemns by belief and unbelief, not ethnicity or nation: Israel's branches were broken off for unbelief, Gentiles are grafted in by faith, and God's children are Abraham's seed by faith.
teachings.text:
**2 Peter 3:9**
*The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.*

**Romans 11:1-5**
*I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin. God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew. Wot ye not what the scripture saith of Elias? how he maketh intercession to God against Israel saying, Lord, they have killed thy prophets, and digged down thine altars; and I am left alone, and they seek my life. But what saith the answer of God unto him? I have reserved to myself seven thousand men, who have not bowed the knee to the image of Baal. Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace.*

It is important to recognize that it isn't by ethnicity or nation that God saves or condemns, but by belief and unbelieving.

The destruction of the Northern Kingdom of Israel was for their unbelief. The eventual destruction of Judea was for rejecting Christ. At the end of the world, on that great and terrible day of the Lord, the wrath will come on the whole earth for unbelief, the righteous remnant spared, and Jesus will get rule with all His saints.

**Romans 11:15-21,30-32**
*For if the casting away of them be the reconciling of the world, what shall the receiving of them be, but life from the dead? For if the firstfruit be holy, the lump is also holy: and if the root be holy, so are the branches. And if some of the branches be broken off, and thou, being a wild olive tree, wert grafted in among them, and with them partakest of the root and fatness of the olive tree; Boast not against the branches. But if thou boast, thou bearest not the root, but the root thee. Thou wilt say then, The branches were broken off, that I might be grafted in. Well; because of unbelief they were broken off, and thou standest by faith. Be not highminded, but fear: For if God spared not the natural branches, take heed lest he also spare not thee.*.. *For as ye in times past have not believed God, yet have now obtained mercy through their unbelief: Even so have these also now not believed, that through your mercy they also may obtain mercy. For God hath concluded them all in unbelief, that he might have mercy upon all.*

The love of God is conditional on belief in His word. The Bible says, without faith it is impossible to please God. His children are children by faith, adopted as sons of God through Christ. Heirs according to His promise, made Abraham's seed for belief.

Those that remain in unbelief are cast into the fire by their own choice. By their own counsels.

teachings.title: Zion, the redeemed bride of Christ
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Zion and Jerusalem are a picture of the believer, the redeemed bride of Christ whom He jealously protects and will perfect as the New Jerusalem.
teachings.text:
But, Zion, like believers, stained crimson in sin, has a redeemer. And, like His church, Jerusalem is His bride, made perfect and decked in the finest array, fit for the King.

**Isaiah 61:10**
*I will greatly rejoice in the Lord, my soul shall be joyful in my God; for he hath clothed me with the garments of salvation, he hath covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decketh himself with ornaments, and as a bride adorneth herself with her jewels.*

**Isaiah 62:1–7**
*For Zion’s sake will I not hold my peace, and for Jerusalem’s sake I will not rest, until the righteousness thereof go forth as brightness, and the salvation thereof as a lamp that burneth. And the Gentiles shall see thy righteousness, and all kings thy glory: and thou shalt be called by a new name, which the mouth of the LORD shall name. Thou shalt also be a crown of glory in the hand of the LORD, and a royal diadem in the hand of thy God. Thou shalt no more be termed Forsaken; neither shall thy land any more be termed Desolate: but thou shalt be called Hephzibah, and thy land Beulah: for the LORD delighteth in thee, and thy land shall be married. For as a young man marrieth a virgin, so shall thy sons marry thee: and as the bridegroom rejoiceth over the bride, so shall thy God rejoice over thee. I have set watchmen upon thy walls, O Jerusalem, which shall never hold their peace day nor night: ye that make mention of the LORD, keep not silence, And give him no rest, till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth.*

Zion, and Jerusalem, are a picture of the believer. A bride of Christ, made precious by His redemption, protecting it like a jealous husband;

**Zechariah 1:14**
*So the angel that communed with me said unto me, Cry thou, saying, Thus saith the Lord of hosts; I am jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion with a great jealousy.*

**Isaiah 54:5–7**
*For thy Maker is thine husband; the LORD of hosts is his name; and thy Redeemer the Holy One of Israel; The God of the whole earth shall he be called. For the LORD hath called thee as a woman forsaken and grieved in spirit, and a wife of youth, when thou wast refused, saith thy God. For a small moment have I forsaken thee; but with great mercies will I gather thee.*

In the end, we shall see New Jerusalem, upon his holy hill, Zion. Perfected as a picture of his people, His bride;

**Revelation 21:1–2**
*And I saw a new heaven and a new earth: for the first heaven and the first earth were passed away; and there was no more sea. And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.*

This is the promise of his holy place, how much more so is it the promise for those who have trusted in Christ. In an unmovable Rock, the cornerstone laid in Zion. The Rock of our salvation, we who are the bride of Christ. Amen

teachings.title: Mount Zion, chosen of God
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Zion is holy because God placed His name there and separated it for His purposes, the place of Christ's sacrifice and future reign, not because its people are holy.
teachings.text:
Mount Zion, Jerusalem, is often referenced and praised as the place God chose to place His name. His holy city, the mountain providing natural protection on 3 sides, situated perfectly. A river running through the fertile valley. The setting where Abraham brought Issac. Where God prepared Himself a sacrifice. Where Jesus was slain and rose again, and where He will reign in the Kingdom to come.

The name, Zion, means a “monument; raised up; sepulcher,” the place of the tomb, hewn out of rock, the site of Christ's burial. Chosen by God.

Jerusalem, the city isn't a lonely peak, but rather a settlement nestled within a protective bowl of higher terrain, with Mt Moriah and the mount of Olives part of the limestone rings, defending the area.

**Psalm 125:1–2**
*They that trust in the LORD shall be as mount Zion, which cannot be removed, but abideth for ever. As the mountains are round about Jerusalem, so the LORD is round about his people from henceforth even for ever.*

Beautiful for situation, a perfect location, the city if the great King on its north face.

**Psalm 132:13–14**
*For the LORD hath chosen Zion; he hath desired it for his habitation. This is my rest for ever: here will I dwell; for I have desired it.*

**1 Peter 2:5–6**
*Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house, an holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God by Jesus Christ. Wherefore also it is contained in the scripture, Behold, I lay in Sion a chief corner stone, elect, precious: and he that believeth on him shall not be confounded.*

The shelter of Zion, the cornerstone of which is Christ, is where Jesus returns to in the end times, with the 144,000 witnesses.

**Revelation 14:1**
*And I looked, and, lo, a Lamb stood on the mount Sion, and with him an hundred forty and four thousand, having his Father’s name written in their foreheads.*

The defenses of this holy mountain were enough to dissuade kings and armies.

Sennacherib, of Assyria, the most powerful emperor of the ancient world, invaded Judah with a massive army of 185,000 soldiers.

He sent his top military commanders to the walls of Jerusalem, fiercely mocking King Hezekiah and blaspheming God, confidently expecting the city to fall just like every other nation before it.

Hezekiah called out to the Lord for protection of the city.

**2 Kings 19:16–19**
*LORD, bow down thine ear, and hear: open, LORD, thine eyes, and see: and hear the words of Sennacherib, which hath sent him to reproach the living God. Of a truth, LORD, the kings of Assyria have destroyed the nations and their lands, And have cast their gods into the fire: for they were no gods, but the work of men’s hands, wood and stone: therefore they have destroyed them. Now therefore, O LORD our God, I beseech thee, save thou us out of his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that thou art the LORD God, even thou only.*

And God harkened to the prayer, for His own purposes and will;

**2 Kings 19:32–34**
*Therefore thus saith the LORD concerning the king of Assyria, He shall not come into this city, nor shoot an arrow there, nor come before it with shield, nor cast a bank against it. By the way that he came, by the same shall he return, and shall not come into this city, saith the LORD. For I will defend this city, to save it, for mine own sake, and for my servant David’s sake.*

Zion is defended for His own sake, because He placed His name there, and for the promise made to David that out of Zion shall come a King.

**Romans 11:26–27**
*And so all Israel shall be saved: as it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob: For this is my covenant unto them, when I shall take away their sins.*

Zion is holy, because it has been separated unto the purposes of God.

It is not holy because the people there are holy. God allowed Babylon to raze the city and remove the people. Jesus decreed that Jerusalem would fall, and in 70AD it did. With the end times approaching, the city is considered wicked;

teachings.title: The inheritance belongs to all in Christ
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: The land promise is fulfilled in the resurrection and the inheritance passes to all who have put on Christ, so Christians who give it away to modern Zionism for politics are like Esau selling his birthright.
teachings.text:
**Hebrews 8:7–10**
*For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second. For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord. For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord; I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people*

The promise to occupy the land will be fulfilled for the Old Testament believers, in the resurrection. The only "Zionism" that matters is Christ Jesus on His throne. The inheritance is passed to all who have put on Christ.

**Romans 8:14–17**
*For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God. For ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear; but ye have received the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father. The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God: And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together*.

This promise, the inheritance and blessings, is the heritage of all believers, from Adam and Abel, Seth and Noah, through every professing Christian today.

The spirit of Esau, who forsook his inheritance for a bowl of pottage, lives in Christians, who for political expediency seek to give it away.

**Hebrews 12:14–17**
*Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord: Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and thereby many be defiled; Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright. For ye know how that afterward, when he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected: for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears.*

This tearful repentance will be the case for many in the end times. Those who placed modern politics and bad theology above the joy unspeakable found in Jesus for all who believe, Jew or Gentile. Man or woman. Bond or free.

teachings.title: The collection was for the saints at Jerusalem
teachings.theme: Zionism refuted
teachings.summary: Romans 15:27 does not oblige Gentile Christians to fund Jews in Israel; it describes one relief gift to saved Christians at Jerusalem.
teachings.text:
We are also told how the charitable relief donated to the church at Jerusalem, mentioned in Romans came to be, that there was a famine, a great dearth throughout the land and the churches of the Gentiles, better off financially, sent them alms.

**Romans 15**
*25 But now I go unto Jerusalem to minister unto the saints.*

*26 For it hath pleased them of Macedonia and Achaia to make a certain contribution for the poor saints which are at Jerusalem.*

*27 It hath pleased them verily; and their debtors they are. For if the Gentiles have been made partakers of their spiritual things, their duty is also to minister unto them in carnal things.*

*28 When therefore I have performed this, and have sealed to them this fruit, I will come by you into Spain.*

I had an (((Adam Green))) disciple, atheist and foolish, taking verse 27 out of context and claiming that it requires save Christian gentiles to support financially Jews in Israel today. Unsaved people with a little knowledge, and without the Spirit to guide them cannot understand scripture and create weird doctrines out of partial verses.

The Bible is telling us that the charity was going to the saved Christians in Jerusalem, not to just any Jews. And more, it is a specific instance and a specific group of people who took it upon themselves to send the relief. Paul isn't even asking the Romans to join them in it.

Do not get your Doctrine from people who are vehemently anti-God and who despise Jesus.

teachings.title: God's promises to Abram, not the modern state
teachings.theme: Zionism refuted
teachings.summary: God's promise to bless them that bless Abram was personal to him, not to the modern Jewish state, and Abram was saved by calling on the Lord.
teachings.text:
All of Genesis, as important as the stories of Adam, Cain, Noah, the flood and Babel are, was prologue to this. The story of Abram and Sarai. Abraham and Sarah.

Up to this point, mankind who called upon the name of the Lord had the promise of His blessing and protection, of God being their savior, but not the specific promise of the man Christ Jesus. Born of man. Seed of Abraham. Here we see that the LORD appears unto Abram and makes him promises.

- I will make of thee a great nation
 - I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing
- I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee:
- and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.

These are direct blessings and promises to Abram, himself. Many try to take the personal promise to Abraham, to bless those that bless him and curse those that curse him, and claim it's an eternal promise to the modern Jew and the apostate state calling itself Israel. This is found no where in Scripture. This is God's promise to protect him and his wife, as God has called Abraham to go to a different land, to Canaan, and there He would establish his legacy.

*And Abram took Sarai his wife, and Lot his brother's son, and all their substance that they had gathered, and the souls that they had gotten in Haran; and they went forth to go into the land of Canaan.*

There, God appeared again to him, and gave this more specific promise; *Unto thy seed will I give this land: and there builded he an altar unto the Lord, who appeared unto him.* *And Abram called upon the name of the Lord.*

He was saved by faith through grace. Note the timing of when that was. It comes up later in scripture.

This promise was made to a 75yr old, childless Abram in a place where *the Canaanite was then in the land.* His altar built between the Mediterranean and Jordan, between Galelee and Jerusalem.

The LORD appearing to Abraham is considered by many to be an Old Testament appearance of Jesus. A theophany. As the Bible says at no time has man seen the Father, many consider the appearance of God unto man in the OT a representation of Christ, who was from the beginning with God and is God.

Next we are given a familiar story of a famine in the land, of going to Egypt to sojourn. Of Pharoah and plagues. This theme of finding refuge and sojourning in Egypt is a picture of young Jesus being taken there by Joseph, just as Jesus' stepfather's namesake will.

There in Egypt, worried that Sarai, his 65yo wife, who was still apparently very fair to look upon, would be taken from him, and that he would be killed, Abram tells her to lie and say they are siblings.

This seems to be a lack of faith by Abram, and causes enmity with Pharoah, who indeed was going to seek to betroth Sarai, but now, subject to plagues by the LORD, angrily asks them to leave the shelter of his kingdom.

God cursed those who would curse Abram, despite his lapse of faith. God made that promise to him, and if he trusted God, he wouldn't fear for his life. As it stood, God came through anyway, but Abram and all his household were sent away back to Canaan and the famine.

teachings.title: Dispensationalists selling the birthright to spiritual Edom
teachings.theme: Zionism refuted
teachings.summary: God did not replace Edom; the Christ-rejecting Jews are spiritual Edom, and dispensationalists who honour them sell their own birthright for man's approval.
teachings.text:
God didn't "replace" Esau with Jacob. Edom with Israel. The choice is made in man's heart.

And the Jews who killed Jesus and the prophets and persecuted the Gentiles who received the inheritance in faith, are spiritually Edom. The wrath of God abides upon them to the uttermost. They are a byword and a parable. A warning.

Modern, dispensationalist Christians who have elevated Jews to coequal status, even giving them honor as "older brothers," claiming that inheritance of the flesh, in the law means they retain the birthright and blessing they rejected when they reject Christ, are carnal and risk going the way of Edom themselves.

They so despise their birthright in Christ they are willing to give it up to Jews for a morsel. For less than a bowl of pottage.
