They say the "church age" ends in failure. Taken up in a pre-trib rapture to make way for the Jews to receive the Kingdom that is ours in Jesus' name. They question the judgment of God and ignore these warnings found throughout the Bible, in exchange for...what? The false teachers get paid. Hagee and the televangelists and evangelical pastors who promote dispensationalism get filthy lucre, for sure. Vipers being rewarded in the flesh. But the flock, many who are believers, they get nothing of value but the brief and fleeting feeling of approval by a group of people who resent and hate them. "If I bless them I will be blessed!" If you are saved in Christ you've already been blessed! If you live in the spirit, doing the will of the Father, the blessings are ours, in abundance.

But for the meaningless approval of man, they sell it all to the wicked, spiritual Edomites.

And like Esau, they will see eventually that their choice robbed them of the blessings, and with tears they will repent, but it will be too late.

teachings.title: Covenants have conditions: the fall of Edom
teachings.theme: Zionism refuted
teachings.summary: God gave Edom a promised land then destroyed it for its iniquities, showing covenants have conditions, against the Zionist claim that God's land promise is unconditional.
teachings.text:
One thing to note regarding God's destruction of Edom, this follows hundreds of years of blessing them with the land of Seir which was promised unto Esau. But their betrayals against Israel, worship of false gods, taking advantage to raid Jerusalem with the Babylonians, it was enough and God took their land and made it desolate.

So many dispensationalists rest their Zionism on "God keeps His promises!" with no recognition or understanding that covenants have conditions. That God judges nations on earth. Here we have an example of a promised land, kept by God, given warning by God through David, and ultimately destroyed for their iniquities.

teachings.title: The Synagogue of Satan Persecuted Smyrna
teachings.theme: Zionism refuted
teachings.summary: Christ calls those who say they are Jews and are not the synagogue of Satan, which Zionist and dispensational churches fail to see.
teachings.text:
*And unto the angel of the church in Smyrna write; These things saith the first and the last, which was dead, and is alive;*

Again, addressing the church of Smyrna, as the *first and the last, which was dead and is alive*. This is Jesus. Alpha and Omega. The risen Christ.

*I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty, (but thou art rich) and I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan. Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life.*

The church at Smyrna is poor, but rich in spirit. They are working for Christ and being persecuted for it by the Jews, so-called. The synagogue of Satan.

The absolute failure of those churches that teach Zionism and dispensationalism, Hebrew roots and other Judaizing heresies to recognize precisely who Jesus is talking about here - **HINT: they call themselves Jews and meet in synagogues** - that failing is the work of Satan in them. They are enemies of God, contrary to all men, and they kill and persecute the saints, liars and antichrists.

The tribulation they gave the early churches has never stopped.

Here, Christ encourages them that despite the tribulation of being jailed, it will be for ten days, and even if they die for His name they will be rewarded with crowns in heaven for their patience and eternal life for their faith.

*He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; He that overcometh shall not be hurt of the second death*.

Another promise to the saved; we shall not be hurt of the second death, which we will see later in Revelation refers to Hell and the lake of fire. The eternal damnation that those who have not overcome will suffer.

teachings.title: No Promise of a Third Temple
teachings.theme: Zionism refuted
teachings.summary: Scripture promises no third temple after 70 AD; Scofield invented this teaching, and any sacrifices offered by Christ-rejecting Jews would be an abomination.
teachings.text:
Reaching the midpoint of Revelation, we see John receives a rod made of a reed to measure the temple of God, but not the outer court. This is tied in to the 3rd Temple prophecy, commonly used by the Dispensationalists to say it must be rebuilt at some point before the Great Tribulation begins.

A proof text offered for the building of the 3rd Temple comes from **Haggai 2:7-9**: *And I will shake all nations, and the desire of all nations shall come: and I will fill this house with glory, saith the Lord of hosts. The silver is mine, and the gold is mine, saith the Lord of hosts. The glory of this latter house shall be greater than of the former, saith the Lord of hosts: and in this place will I give peace, saith the Lord of hosts*.

Other than this, there is no scripture that promises any new temple will be built in Jerusalem after God used Rome to destroy it in 70AD. Scofield, that viper, is one of the primary sources of this understanding, and his study notes have deceived millions over the past century. Jews in the Tanya, a book of the Chabad Lubavitch Zionist Jews, also claims that Jews will rule the world when the temple is rebuilt and their Moshiach comes.

It's possible. There's obviously attempts to get the Temple Mount cleared of the mosque that currently occupies it. There are fund raising efforts by evangelicals and hyperdispensationalist false prophets, saying they are going to rebuild.

The argument that some form of a temple must be built comes from **Daniel 9:27** regarding the antichrist and the takeover of Jerusalem:

*And he shall confirm the covenant with many for one week: and in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease, and for the overspreading of abominations he shall make it desolate, even until the consummation, and that determined shall be poured upon the desolate*.

Basically, the antichrist and the Jews are allies for a year, before he turns on them and will cause offerings of sacrifices to stop, and raise the abomination of desolation in their midst. The argument is, no temple, how could there be sacrifices?

We will see in the second half of Revelation that there will be a New Jerusalem, adorned like a bride and given to Jesus as in a wedding. The old Jerusalem is not really important. As John writes a few verses later, Jerusalem is spiritually called *Sodom and Egypt*, *where also our Lord was crucified.*

God's not a fan.

It is entirely possible the destruction in 70AD and the ceasing of sacrifices and oblations is part of a dual fulfilment. It's difficult to say. We can just go by what is in God's word, and it isn't entirely clear.

One thing that is for certain, if the dispies are correct and the Jews manage to build a 3rd temple and begin making sacrifices there, it will not be pleasing to the Lord. They won't be to Him, as they have not the Son, neither the Father. The sacrifice was always a picture of Christ. If they worship there, it will be itself an abomination and the animals sacrificed to Satan.

teachings.title: The Woman Is Not Modern Israel
teachings.theme: Zionism refuted
teachings.summary: Scofield's teaching that the woman is Israel twists Joseph's dream to prop up a pre-trib rapture and Jewish kingdom, while Revelation mentions Jews only as persecutors.
teachings.text:
Just to reiterate, the Scofield view that the woman is Israel, in order to maintain the Dispensationalist view of end times Bible prophecy, is wrong. Nothing about it fits other than the 12 stars of the crown, the moon and sun, and even that is a stretch.

They use as proof text the story of Joseph and his dreams from **Genesis 37**:

*And he dreamed yet another dream, and told it his brethren, and said, Behold, I have dreamed a dream more; and, behold, the sun and the moon and the eleven stars made obeisance to me. And he told it to his father, and to his brethren: and his father rebuked him, and said unto him, What is this dream that thou hast dreamed? Shall I and thy mother and thy brethren indeed come to bow down ourselves to thee to the earth? And his brethren envied him; but his father observed the saying.*

This dream puts Joseph as the focus of the worship by his brothers and parents. His father, a man, was Israel. Not a woman. The stars were not a crown. The sun and moon may have been Jacob and Rachel, but again, the presence of a sun and moon as clothing on the woman doesn't work, as Jesus human lineage is through Leah to Judah.

This interpretation doesn't make any sense. But they need it to be modern Israel in order to make the prophecy that follows of a pre-trib rapture and Jewish earthly kingdom, fit. Like most all of their Zionist heresy, they have to take liberties with literal scripture and lean on interpretation of symbolic verses to make it all work. And they will say in no uncertain terms that their interpretation of this chapter and who the woman is as the only correct one.

*Now is come salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of his Christ: for the accuser of our brethren is cast down, which accused them before our God day and night. And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony; and they loved not their lives unto the death...And the dragon was wroth with the woman, and went to make war with the remnant of her seed, which keep the commandments of God, and have the testimony of Jesus Christ.*

Modern Israel and the Jews who are only mentioned in Revelation in a negative light, as persecuting the saints in a like manner with Satan's war upon believers and are called a Synagogue of Satan. That's it. Every other prophecy and promise is to believers, of every kindred and tongue.

The worship of Jews and their god, Satan, is the entire point of dispensationalism and Scofield's twisted interpretation of the Bible.

teachings.title: I Regarded Them Not
teachings.theme: Zionism refuted
teachings.summary: Hebrews 8:9 shows the Jews broke the covenant and God regarded them not, so salvation was never by bloodline but always by faith.
teachings.text:
The entire New Testament is a case against dispensationalism and the idea that Jews are still "chosen," and exempt from the faith of Christ unto forgiveness that is the New Testament, the *better* covenant. But Hebrews 8:9 is one of many silver bullets, putting down the heretical idea that Jews today are special:

*Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord.*

God's covenants, His promises to a nation, like all covenants, carry if-then statements that if not fulfilled, exempt the parties from its terms. The Lord says here in no uncertain terms that the Jews continued not in His covenant AND I REGARDED THEM NOT.

It can't be any plainer. Just as John the Baptist says to the Pharisees, *Think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.*

It was never about genetics or bloodlines, except so far as the promise of Christ, which wasn't to the Jews but to all men. The root and the seed.

And salvation from Hell and death was always by faith, calling upon the name of the Lord. But the law that served to convict those who transgressed, a schoolmaster, is replaced by the law in man's heart, and the knowledge of the truth in Christ Jesus.

The Old Testament then, which some still believed they were under as Paul wrote this, was ready to vanish away.

teachings.title: God is able of these stones to raise children
teachings.theme: Zionism refuted
teachings.summary: John the Baptist rebuked the Jews for trusting their lineage from Abraham, repudiating the special treatment for the Jews that dispensationalists still teach.
teachings.text:
Here in Luke chapter 3, we find his goal, stated in the opening of his Gospel to "*set forth in order a declaration of those things which are most surely believed among us*," being met, giving precise details to the time in which John the Baptist, followed by Jesus, began their ministry. Luke establishes who was in charge, and where, pinpointing for readers the time and place of this happening, with familiar figures of their recent past; *That thou mightest know the certainty of those things, wherein thou hast been instructed.*

And so we find John, born roughly 6 months ahead of Jesus, has fufifiled the prophecy given his father by Gabriel, to be the answer to the prophecy given Isaiah; the voice in the wilderness making straight the paths of the Lord.

In the times before modernity, when the lords and kings would travel abroad, often in caravans, taking weeks or months to get where they were going, a group of their servants would run ahead, both to herald their lord's passing to prepare those in the path chosen to receive their king, and to make certain the road was clear. That the way was smooth. Harbingers and workmen.

So too, Christ the Lord was coming and the paths were to be made straight for Him.

In scripture, we often see the idea of walking in God's statutes, following His wisdom, being righteous by obeying His sayings, is compared to walking a path. Turning neither to the left not right. But following the narrow way of the Lord.

John, the harbinger of the Lord is sent by God to spiritually make straight the paths, to bring the people to repentance, turning towards His Son. Baptizing those who believed, a picture of Christ's crucifixion, burial and resurrection, and a symbol of their being washed clean by the remission of sins. Preparing them that shall see the salvation of God among them. Exhorting those who were saved to now do the works meet for repentance. Charity. Proper living. Changed as those who are free from the wrath should live.

John is filled with the Holy Ghost, as promised, and speaks boldly and with authority the words of God. He is the first prophet of the Lord to have the Holy Ghost upon him in 400 years. His hard preaching against sin and of the word of God, scripture, draws people from all over the region.

We see the lands mentioned by ruler, and it encompasses all of Judea, up into Samaria and the provinces from the sea and in and around Jordan, and it is from these places that multitudes come to hear John preach and to be baptized.

In **Matthew 3** we see that this draws attention of the Pharisees and Sadducees, and that the preaching he does, also shown in **Luke 3**, is an indictment of the Jews, especially their religious leaders.

*O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come? Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance: And think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.*

John speaking in the Spirit says that if they are truly there repentant of their false ways, show the fruit of it. Especially the religious leaders who have not the fruits, the souls prepared to repent towards God. They've failed the people. They have rested on the fact that they are God's "chosen." They haven't prepared anyone for the salvation to come.

This generation of vipers has believed that by the nature of their lineage they would be saved. This is the same mistaken idea behind dispensationalism and the "God's not done with the Jews!" mentality among so many misguided and judaized Christians today.

But John repudiates the idea of special treatment for the Jews. He says God could raise up Israelites from rocks if He so chose. They aren't special boys. And they certainly aren't living in a manner that shows God-fearing reverence for Him and His laws.

teachings.title: There is no respect of persons with God
teachings.theme: Zionism refuted
teachings.summary: Jew and Gentile face the same judgment and revelation, refuting the dispensational idea that Jews are favoured by God.
teachings.text:
Again this argument Paul is making is to provoke the Jews to jealousy and into separation towards the Gospel, and to reject being holier than thou against the repentant pagans being converted in Rome. But this entire exchange is also important to understand when dealing with Zionism and the Dispensationalist error that Jews are favored by God.

There is no respect of persons to God.

The Jew and Gentile are judged the same. Given the same revelation of wrath. Have the law in their hearts, given a conscience, the Spirit working to convict them of sin. All to bring them to the knowledge of the truth, that salvation comes by Christ and the Gospel. By the spirit of the law, not the letter.

All face the same judgment. None have an excuse. And our following the letter of the law doesn't make us better than those who aren't where we are spiritually. Only the grace of God is keeping us from the same fate.

This doesn't mean we don't judge, it means we should try to judge righteously as God has with us.

And never think you are a special boy, given favor by God for who you are, what tribe you're born to, how diligently you keep the letter of the law, but remaining humble in the grace of God.

teachings.title: Let their eyes be darkened
teachings.theme: Zionism refuted
teachings.summary: The prophets and Jesus cursed unbelieving Israel, and bless them that bless thee is fulfilled in Christ, not in anyone calling himself a Jew.
teachings.text:
As David wrote, cursing Israel in **Psalm 69**; *Let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see, and bow down their back alway.*

(Note all the cursing of Israel in the prophets and Jesus' preaching. They were not afraid of being cursed for it. The "bless them that bless thee, curse them that curse thee" being fufiled in Jesus, not anyone calling themselves Jew)

Paul hopes that, as God said repeatedly in the OT through the prophets, He will provoke them to jealousy by the salvation of the Gentiles. By giving the Kingdom to another people, they will repent.

Paul says that if God is glorified in the salvation of the Gentiles by the destruction of the Jews, imagine how much more glory God would have if the Jews as a nation, would repent and believe?

teachings.title: The alms for Jerusalem were for believing saints
teachings.theme: Zionism refuted
teachings.summary: The collection for the poor saints at Jerusalem was temporary relief for believing brethren in a famine, not a mandate for Christians to fund unbelieving Jews forever.
teachings.text:
As Paul begins to wrap up the letter with his intentions to visit the churches in Rome, which he will eventually if not in the manner he thinks as he wrote this, he delves into some of the plans he has made that will delay his journey.

One of those things is the bringing of alms to the church at Jerusalem, collected from the churches throughout Asia Minor and Greece to benefit the believers there suffering through a great famine, as we were shown in **Acts 11**:

*And in these days came prophets from Jerusalem unto Antioch. And there stood up one of them named Agabus, and signified by the Spirit that there should be great dearth throughout all the world: which came to pass in the days of Claudius Caesar. Then the disciples, every man according to his ability, determined to send relief unto the brethren which dwelt in Judaea*.

This is discussed in other epistles, and is very specific to the time and place and need. It is about saved brethren in the Jerusalem of that time, in the famine that plagued the land as it drew nearer and nearer to its destruction. Relief from the other churches of believers, that the brethren of saved believing Jews and others in that church may ride out the hardship to the glory of God.

Many enemies of the Gospel take the following verses from **Romans 15** and twist them into something else;

*But now I go unto Jerusalem to minister unto the saints. For it hath pleased them of Macedonia and Achaia to make a certain contribution for the poor saints which are at Jerusalem. It hath pleased them verily; and their debtors they are. For if the Gentiles have been made partakers of their spiritual things, their duty is also to minister unto them in carnal things.*

Unbelieving Jews twist this to guilt Christians into supporting all Jews. All the time. Begging for money in the most obscene ways, and tricking those weak in the faith into thinking they are mandated to fund "Israel" forever.

But we have been made partakers of their spiritual things only in Christ. The need was temporary. For believers. Brethren caught in the midst of God's wrath upon the rest of the Jews.

Others cite this passage in the same manner as the unrepentant Jews, claiming we are cucked by our faith, and required to serve Jews. This isn't the case and it is always interesting to me how much in common Jews and pagan Gentiles have in regards to their abuse of scripture to tell us what we believe.

teachings.title: We have Abraham to our father
teachings.theme: Zionism refuted
teachings.summary: The claim that the Jews inherit the land as Abraham's many children is the false basis of Zionism, since the promises were always conditional on obedience to God's covenant.
teachings.text:
**Ezekiel 33** concludes, the destruction of Jerusalem has happened. One who escaped comes to the prophet in the evening and tells him, but the hand of God keeps Ezekiel from responding until the morning came, and he was no longer struck dumb. And he receives the word of God.

The Lord says that those from the wastes and wilderness of Judah, who escaped out of the desolation of Jerusalem speak, saying that because Abraham was one, and was promised land, that they being many deserve the inheritance.

This is the argument made by Jews today. The basis of Zionism. The false doctrine that because they are children of the law, and many, the promise of the land given Abraham should apply even more so to them.

**Matthew 3:9**
*And think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.*

The promises and inheritance was never given a people because of who they were. But by the condition of what they did. A condition repeatedly given.

**Exodus 19:5**
*Now therefore, if ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people: for all the earth is mine*

**Hebrews 8:7-9**
*For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second. For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord.*

The word of the Lord upon Ezekiel stresses these same points. They are filled with violence and Idolatry and adultery and abominations.

For this, God says He will lay the land most desolate because of their abominations. Then they shall know He is the Lord.

teachings.title: The promise was to Abraham's seed, which is Christ
teachings.theme: Zionism refuted
teachings.summary: The promise to Abraham was made to his seed Christ and to all who are in Christ, the land promise was fulfilled under Joshua and kept conditionally under the Mosaic covenant, so Zionism wrongly gives the inheritance to unbelieving Jews.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 48** broadly captures the grandeur and love of God towards His holy land. This love is seen long before Israel as a nation enters in, or even exists. It was in the beginning, when God promised a land to Abraham.

**Genesis 12:1–3**
*Now the LORD had said unto Abram, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father’s house, unto a land that I will shew thee: And I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing: And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.*

The promise to Abraham was both for the land, and the Christ. Long before the exodus. Long before the wandering. Before Isaac was ever born, the land that would become Israel, the province of Judah, the city of Jerusalem, in the mountains of Zion, was set apart for God.

The blessings and inheritance made to Abraham, who believed God and it was counted for righteousness, was made to him and his seed. Jesus Christ.

**Galatians 3:16**
*Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ.*

Zionism is a modern political ideology that takes the promise to Abraham, and rather than give the inheritance and blessing to Christ, and all who are in Christ, gives it to unbelieving, apostate Jews.

**Galatians 3:27–29**
*For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus. And if ye be Christ’s, then are ye Abraham’s seed, and heirs according to the promise.*

The claim for the children of Israel to the land, by promise of God, was fulfilled in the time of Joshua.

**Joshua 21:43–45**
*And the LORD gave unto Israel all the land which he sware to give unto their fathers; and they possessed it, and dwelt therein. And the LORD gave them rest round about, according to all that he sware unto their fathers: and there stood not a man of all their enemies before them; the LORD delivered all their enemies into their hand. There failed not ought of any good thing which the LORD had spoken unto the house of Israel; all came to pass.*

The promise to Abraham was unconditional. But the promise made to Moses by God in the wilderness, for His people to occupy His land, was conditional.

**Deuteronomy 28:63–64**
*And it shall come to pass, that as the LORD rejoiced over you to do you good, and to multiply you; so the LORD will rejoice over you to destroy you, and to bring you to nought; and ye shall be plucked from off the land whither thou goest to possess it. And the LORD shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.*

Many Christians today will say "God keeps His promises! The Jews deserve this land!" They place political Zionism and the ethnic ultranationalism of the modern Jewish state as being part of an unconditional and irrevocable covenant with the people by heritage and genealogy.

But the Bible is clear, that the covenant made in the wilderness was explicitly conditional, that what was given to the people through Moses could not, by their failure, disannul the promise made to Abraham and his singular seed.

**Galatians 3:17–18**
*And this I say, that the covenant, that was confirmed before of God in Christ, the law, which was four hundred and thirty years after, cannot disannul, that it should make the promise of none effect. For if the inheritance be of the law, it is no more of promise: but God gave it to Abraham by promise.*

But the covenant made those 430 years after Abraham? It has faded away, replace by a better covenant with better promises, to all who are in Christ, regardless of their ethnicity or origin.

teachings.title: The cursed fig tree withered from the roots
teachings.theme: Judgment on unbelieving Jerusalem
teachings.summary: The fruitless fig tree pictures Judah, cut off forever for bearing no fruit, which is not replacement theology and refutes the dispensational claim that God is not done with the Jews.
teachings.text:
The chapter opens with Mark's telling of what is popularly known as Palm Sunday, though it occured on a Saturday. The Jerusalem crowd hailing Jesus, riding on the colt of an ass as in prophecy, as he arrives for the Passover, of which He will be the sacrifice.

The colt is there where He said, and they allow the disciples to take it, as He said. Because everything in this world is God's and His to use for His glory.

Then we have a telling of the fruitless fig tree. Jesus, seeking fruit finds none and curses the tree that it will produce no fruit forever after, and the tree is withered and destroyed from its root.

*No man eat fruit of thee hereafter for ever... And in the morning, as they passed by, they saw the fig tree dried up from the roots. And Peter calling to remembrance saith unto him, Master, behold, the fig tree which thou cursedst is withered away.*

It is not "replacement theology," it is the taking away of the Kingdom for failing to provide fruit, not bringing souls meet for repentance unto salvation. For rejecting the stone, cut without hands, laid as the cornerstone before the foundation of the world.

For the "God's not done with the Jews!" false doctrine, this story is twisted, because a plain reading is perfectly understandable. We see more in **Matthew 23;**

*And when he saw a fig tree in the way, he came to it, and found nothing thereon, but leaves only, and said unto it, Let no fruit grow on thee henceforward for ever. And presently the fig tree withered away.*

This is a literal story that holds obvious symbolism regarding the Jews, here at the end of Christ's earthly ministry. Fruit, as always in the Gospel, means saved believers, those faithful to God and saved by His promise, in His Son, Jesus.

It's reminiscent of a parable in **Luke 13:6-9**;

*He spake also this parable; A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard; and he came and sought fruit thereon, and found none.Then said he unto the dresser of his vineyard, Behold, these three years I come seeking fruit on this fig tree, and find none: cut it down; why cumbereth it the ground? And he answering said unto him, Lord, let it alone this year also, till I shall dig about it, and dung it: And if it bear fruit, well: and if not, then after that thou shalt cut it down.*

The tree is Judah. The Lord, God the Father, the dresser, Jesus Christ. His earthly ministry, to the lost sheep of Israel was the final attempt to produce fruit of that tree. And having no more fruit, it was cut down and destroyed.

God's word is clear, it is forever that the tree is destroyed. It is cut down. It is cast into the fire. Never to bloom again.

The dispensationalist lies are built on denying scripture.

teachings.title: The Days of Vengeance on Judea
teachings.theme: Judgment on unbelieving Jerusalem
teachings.summary: In Luke 21 Jesus speaks of the Jews as they and them in the days of vengeance, matching the Gentiles treading Jerusalem in Revelation 11.
teachings.text:
**Luke 21**

2*0 And when ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh.*

*21 Then let them which are in Judaea flee to the mountains; and let them which are in the midst of it depart out; and let not them that are in the countries enter thereinto.*

*22 For these be the days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled.*

*23 But woe unto them that are with child, and to them that give suck, in those days! for there shall be great distress in the land, and wrath upon this people.*

*24 And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.*

The Olivette discourse in Luke, which Jesus gives us details of the end times contains this passage regarding the days of vengeance, where those who are within Judea are destroyed. Now. Of course, dual fulfillment aside, this fits in with Revelation 11 and the Gentiles trampling the holy city underfoot.

It's interesting that Jesus refers to these people, they, and them. Talking of the Jews as another, whereas believers He will say thee, ye and thou.

But here Jesus describes the invasion and destruction of the Jews which corresponds with the beast and his armies eliminating them in the end times during the wrath period of the second three and a half years.

teachings.title: Your house is left unto you desolate
teachings.theme: Judgment on unbelieving Jerusalem
teachings.summary: Jesus' lament over Jerusalem which killed the prophets marks His being through with those reprobates, who would not see Him until the day of wrath.
teachings.text:
*The same day there came certain of the Pharisees, saying unto him, Get thee out, and depart hence: for Herod will kill thee.*

The spiteful Jews of Galelee threatening that Herod was looking to kill Jesus, that they would get Him to leave. He laughingly says tell that old fox that He still doing work and will abide a while. He's got devils to cast out and people to heal, that He'd be finished in three days. Showing no fear, because Jesus knows where and when His death should come.

And, because Jerusalem is where the Jews always killed the prophets, He says to the Pharisees *it cannot be that a prophet perish out of Jerusalem.* It is a slam against them, and must have pricked their hearts with shame and anger.

*O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, which killest the prophets, and stonest them that are sent unto thee; how often would I have gathered thy children together, as a hen doth gather her brood under her wings, and ye would not! Behold, your house is left unto you desolate: and verily I say unto you, Ye shall not see me, until the time come when ye shall say, Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.*

He is through with these reprobates. He is done, saying you won't see Me until the day of the Lord. The time of wrath. When every knee shall bow. He tried to get them to believe but they would not. And now, they are done. Twice-dead. Cut off. His destiny drawing near, but theirs is present before them. Weeping and gnashing of teeth, cast out into outer darkness in the lake of fire.

teachings.title: His blood be on us: the Jews crucified Christ
teachings.theme: Judgment on unbelieving Jerusalem
teachings.summary: The Gospels show the Jews, not the Romans, demanded Christ's death, and Jesus prophesied judgment on them as the old covenant was done away at the cross.
teachings.text:
And so we see the multitudes of the Jews come up from the High Priest's home, to be accused before Pilate that the Romans may kill Jesus for them.

Pilate examines Jesus and says to the chief priests and to the people, I find no fault in this man. Jesus is the lamb without blemish.

And hearing that Jesus is of Galilee, not of Judea, and having Herod who is protectorate of that region in Jerusalem for the feasts, sends Jesus unto him. Herod too finds no fault with Christ Jesus, but his men shamefully mock Him, dressing this "King of the Jews" in purple, as the Jews slander and bear false witness that Jesus may be slain. Returning to Pilate, he calls the Jews accusing Jesus to him, saying, *Ye have brought this man unto me, as one that perverteth the people: and, behold, I, having examined him before you, have found no fault in this man touching those things whereof ye accuse him.* And was to give Jesus stripes as chastisement, but the Roman governor was to set Jesus free.

But the Jews insisted, "Crucify Him!"

This Biblical truth is considered "antisemetic blood libel" today, in many supposed Christian churches. You will see this today, as various priests and pastors will make public statement and social media posts blaming the Romans for the death of Christ.

But the Gospels tell the truth. In **John 18**:

*Then said Pilate unto them, Take ye him, and judge him according to your law. The Jews therefore said unto him, It is not lawful for us to put any man to death.*

In Matthew 27:

*Then answered all the people, and said, His blood be on us, and on our children.*

**John 19**
*But they cried out, Away with him, away with him, crucify him. Pilate saith unto them, Shall I crucify your King? The chief priests answered, We have no king but Caesar.*

And as Jesus says to the mournful women of Jerusalem, here in **Luke 23**, as He carries His cross, beaten bloody, face unrecognizable, stripes on His back bleeding so much they pressed Simon of Cyrene to help bring the cross up the hill; Jesus says:
*Daughters of Jerusalem, weep not for me, but weep for yourselves, and for your children. For, behold, the days are coming, in the which they shall say, Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that never bare, and the paps which never gave suck.Then shall they begin to say to the mountains, Fall on us; and to the hills, Cover us. For if they do these things in a green tree, what shall be done in the dry?*

Remember, that the spring feasts and holy days, the first of which being Passover and the feast of unleavened bread, represents Jesus Christ and His first coming. The time of green wood, newly budded. The fall feasts, with the trumpets and harvest, the time of dry trees, which are kindled for fire. Here we see Jesus' prophecy against the Jews in the end times, even as He is led to His death by them.

It is undeniable that the people who were chosen by God to be His ministers of the Gospel to all the world, who had a covenant to be His people, a holy nation, an example and light unto the world bringing repentance and salvation, utterly rejected their inheritance, and so, with their killing Jesus the veil in the temple was torn in two. The Old Testament done away with. Its ordinances nailed to the cross with Christ.

teachings.title: A Jew is defined by rejecting Christ
teachings.theme: Judgment on unbelieving Jerusalem
teachings.summary: Modern Jews are defined by their rejection of Christ and are like a put-away unfaithful wife, while God has taken believers as His people.
teachings.text:
This ties in with the study of Jeremiah. Jews, modern people calling themselves Jews, are defined by their rejection of Jesus as the Christ.

Regardless of genetic background, origin story, current ideology or religion, or anything else, a Jew is defined by their utter rejection of Christ and the God of their fathers.

And by this, they are as the unfaithful wife, of a whoring with false gods and badmouthing their former Husband, Who has put them away and taken to Him another people, who believe on His word. And call upon the name of the Lord.

There can be no peace with these people. Just as an ex-wife of a bitter divorce cannot have peace with the new wife, loyal and true. Sealed by the Spirit and circumcised of the heart with the circumcision made without hands.

teachings.title: Reprobate silver: Jerusalem as dross
teachings.theme: Judgment on unbelieving Jerusalem
teachings.summary: Jerusalem broke the old covenant through idolatry, false prophets and oppressing the poor, despised God's longsuffering, and was judged and cast out like dross, which is why a new covenant was needed.
teachings.text:
We see here in the preaching against Jerusalem, where the Lord demands the prophet tell the Jews of their abominations and His judgment, that much of it mirrors those things given to Moses in the wilderness. The things God proclaimed should be dealt with by death. That the blood be upon the wicked and not on the people in the land.

But the children of Israel failed to uphold their end of the covenant and now faced the promised judgment.

**Hebrews 8:7-9**
*For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second. For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah: Not according to the covenant that I Made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord.*

The longsuffering of God, that nearly 1,000 years passed from Sinai and the law to the utter destruction of Jerusalem, was taken by the people to mean God wasn't present. That He no longer cared. That maybe He wasn't real.

His mercy and calls to repentance, ignored. The grace He offers men because of His love, taken advantage of. For greed and lust.

And false prophets preaching lies, saying "The Lord has spoken," when He hadn't. And devouring widow's houses and taking advantage of the poor and the fatherless.

**Matthew 23:13-15**
*But woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men: for ye neither go in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering to go in. Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye devour widows' houses, and for a pretence make long prayer: therefore ye shall receive the greater damnation. Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made, ye make him twofold more the child of hell than yourselves*.

The Lord looked for the righteous to be the salt that preserves, and found none. Just like in Sodom, where He told Moses if there were found just 10 righteous men, He would spare the cities. And so He promises to gather the wicked and melt them in flame like the molten metals they make their abominations with. For sacrifice in the mountains. For their idolatry, for their shedding of blood. For their degeneracy. Extortion, usury, greed.

They have become as dross. Impurities in the silver, cast out.

**Jeremiah 6:30**
*Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the Lord hath rejected them.*

teachings.title: No chosen people but in Christ
teachings.theme: Dispensationalism refuted
teachings.summary: Paul refutes the idea that Jews are God's chosen and Gentile believers lesser, there is only the one dispensation of grace, and Rome's sin of presumption keeps people from assurance.
teachings.text:
Again the focus of these first 3 chapters is attacking the idea that Jews are God's "chosen people," and that Gentile believers are somehow less-than in their inheritance. Paul puts this false notion to bed, emphatically. We are the second born who received the full inheritance and blessing. The Jews having sold it in their fornication for the pottage of earthly things.

Dispensationalists rely on the appearance of the word 'dispensation' in these passages, to justify their wicked heresy, while the text of it destroys them. There is only the dispensation of grace. The change is to extend it to all men, through Jesus Christ regardless of lineage.

There is no limit to the atonement, but the free will to believe the Gospel by those that receive it, and *In whom we have boldness and access with confidence by the faith of him.*

This destroys the damnable "mortal sin of presumption" made by the Catholic Church to snare the unsuspecting into never coming to salvation, and never having that confidence, put in bondage to dead works of the law, and reliant on the RCC to save them in the end. Sending millions to Hell.

teachings.title: Wrath is come upon them to the uttermost
teachings.theme: Unbelieving Jews a synagogue of Satan
teachings.summary: Paul's words that the Jews killed the Lord, please not God and are contrary to all men still describe them today, whatever their origin, as a synagogue of Satan.
teachings.text:
Of the Jews, Paul doesn't mince words;

*Who both killed the Lord Jesus, and their own prophets, and have persecuted us; and they please not God, and are contrary to all men: Forbidding us to speak to the Gentiles that they might be saved, to fill up their sins alway: for the wrath is come upon them to the uttermost.*

This is still true of the Jews today. This is who they are and why they are like they are, regardless of the origin story we might believe. Regardless which Kaiser Sose-jewish myth they perpetrate regarding who they are, the truth is that God's wrath is upon them to the uttermost, because they do not please Him, prevent Gentiles from hearing the truth of Jesus, and are contrary to all men.

Edomite, Khazarian, Ashkenaz, Cain, Canaanite; Adamic or not. This is who they are. It is important to recognize the biblical perspective, as it cuts through the noise and gets down to what matters. They are a synagogue of Satan.

teachings.title: Not replacement but rejection
teachings.theme: Spiritual Edom
teachings.summary: Like Esau the Jews despised their birthright by rejecting Christ and became spiritual Edom, which is rejection, not replacement, the younger receiving the blessing by faith.
teachings.text:
Now, the Bible says that God hated Esau, and Jacob He loved. This is referring to the nations that come from each, Jacob giving birth to the 12 patriarchs of Israel, Esau the nations of Edomites. Much is made of this distinction, but the fate of Edom is not necessarily reflected in the life of its patriarch, Esau. In the next chapter we will look more closely at that.

For now, the parallels to Cain and Abel, Sarah and Hagar, Isaac and Ismael, Jews and Gentiles, even Jesus and Barabbas, the free will choices given to show that God favors faith over the law, spirit over the flesh, blesses them that trust His promises and do His will, giving them the inheritance for their faith, and the casting out of those who are after the flesh, even if by law they have a birthright claim.

The entire Old Testament serves as a pattern for the salvation to come offered in Christ. Both the choice to believe, placing faith above flesh, explaining the theology of the New Testament with examples from the Old. And continually we see the eldest by law passed over, to serve the younger, who by faith receives both the birthright and blessing.

When applied to the Jews and Gentiles, this is called "replacement theology," which is a misnomer. Like Esau, Jews sought an earthly kingdom from an earthly messiah, to satisfy their fleshly desires. They sold their birthright, despising their inheritance, by choosing to kill Christ. By rejecting the blessing that had carried them from Canaan to Egypt, back to the promised land. Through wars, invasions and captivity, they lost everything, for the younger, the Gentiles, to gain.

It's not replacement, it's rejection. Spiritual Edom. And like Edom after the flesh, they were made desolate by the Lord.

**Jeremiah 49**

*10 But I have made Esau bare, I have uncovered his secret places, and he shall not be able to hide himself: his seed is spoiled, and his brethren, and his neighbours, and he is not.*

*11 Leave thy fatherless children, I will preserve them alive; and let thy widows trust in me.*

*12 For thus saith the Lord; Behold, they whose judgment was not to drink of the cup have assuredly drunken; and art thou he that shall altogether go unpunished? thou shalt not go unpunished, but thou shalt surely drink of it.*

*13 For I have sworn by myself, saith the Lord, that Bozrah shall become a desolation, a reproach, a waste, and a curse; and all the cities thereof shall be perpetual wastes.*

*14 I have heard a rumour from the Lord, and an ambassador is sent unto the heathen, saying, Gather ye together, and come against her, and rise up to the battle.*

*15 For, lo, I will make thee small among the heathen, and despised among men.*

*16 Thy terribleness hath deceived thee, and the pride of thine heart, O thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, that holdest the height of the hill: though thou shouldest make thy nest as high as the eagle, I will bring thee down from thence, saith the Lord.*

*17 Also Edom shall be a desolation: every one that goeth by it shall be astonished, and shall hiss at all the plagues thereof.*

*18 As in the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah and the neighbour cities thereof, saith the Lord, no man shall abide there, neither shall a son of man dwell in it.*

teachings.title: Who first trusted in Christ
teachings.summary: Ephesians 1 does not teach unconditional election, because the chosen are those who first trusted in Christ, and the elect nation is spiritual Israel, not the Jews of the flesh.
teachings.text:
Here we see in what is considered the strongest case for special boyism undone with one conditional phrase, "who first trusted in Christ."

Ephesians 1 and Romans 8 are the go to chapters used by special boys to justify their being "chosen" for salvation, but both Ephesians 1 and Romans 8 precede Ephesians 2 and Romans 9, the nails in the coffin of dispensationalism, the idea that only the Israel of the flesh were "chosen."

Paul is establishing that the new covenant is for Israel of the spirit, and has to establish that in the same way (saved and unsaved) physical Israel was predestined by God to be used for His purpose, so too saved Gentiles representing spiritual Israel are similarly a chosen nation.

That God in His foreknowledge destined and shaped those who would be heirs to the promise to be His tools on earth. That knowing who would believe and who wouldn't allows Him to craft the believers to be of best use for His will, is almost a secondary point of this scripture.

He's establishing that the Jews who are persecuting saved Gentiles, claiming that Israel of the flesh are still God's special boys and Gentiles aren't heirs to that kingdom or adopted sons of God, are liars.

teachings.title: Reprobate silver: the unbelieving Jews rejected
teachings.summary: He teaches that Paul frames Jewish persecution as reprobate versus elect, that per Jeremiah 6:30 the unbelieving Jews are rejected of God while saved Greek and Jew are now His elect, and that Jewish antichrists are turned over to a reprobate mind.
teachings.text:
Paul is again writing of the reprobate, the rejected of God, and those abominable and disobedient deceivers going after the *elect*, or chosen.

When Paul frequently writes of the Jewish persecution of the faithful, he frames it in terms of the reprobate vs the elect, because he is trying to show the Gentiles that THEY are the chosen people of God now, and the Jews the rejected:

"*Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the Lord hath rejected them."* **Jeremiah 6:30**

This deliberate use is misinterpreted by calvanists who miss the point being made; that Saved Christians, "Greek and Jew" are now God's chosen, His elect, not the unbelieving Jew. And that they in their jealousy and envy, have further become filled with all unrighteousness.

To be a Jew of the flesh after the coming of Christ is to reject God. To not retain Him in their knowledge. Jews whole identity is that rejection, and God's reprobation of them in return.

This is why Jewish antichrists are so wicked. They are turned over to a reprobate mind.

teachings.title: Whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord
teachings.summary: There is no difference between Jew and Greek and no chosen people; every saint from Adam on was saved by believing and calling on the Lord, with nothing added.
teachings.text:
For scripture says "*Whosoever* believeth on Him shall not be ashamed."

And because there is no difference between "Jew and Greek," there is no "chosen people." Dispensationalism rests entirely on the idea that there is, and so they deny the word of God.

*For whosoever call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.*

Adam believed. Able believed. Seth called upon His name. Enoch believed. Noah believed. Abraham believed and it was counted upon him for righteousness. Sara, Issac, Joseph, Moses, Joshua..all OT saints, they all are said to have believed and called upon the name of the Lord.

That's it. There is no "and..."

There is no church you must join, sacrament you must have, no works of the law, no special boy status, no hypocritical "fruit inspection."

 No other act, regardless of zeal and sincere hope in those acts, can save anyone.

teachings.title: Romans 11 and the reprobate nation of Israel
teachings.summary: Paul's argument in Romans 11 is that the remnant are those Jews who believe the Gospel, and that God does not hold out salvation indefinitely but cuts off the unbelieving, whether individuals or a nation, and turns them over to reprobation.
teachings.text:
Here in Romans 11, Paul is finishing the JQ begun in chapter 9 and 10, as it pertains to Israel after the flesh, the nation, now that Christ had come.

This builds on the theme he has from the start; that all men are without excuse in condemnation, and further some men and nations condemn themselves by bringing God to reject them utterly, unto reprobation. That even with the law, the Jews were condemned and without it, so were the Gentiles. That the Gospel of faith alone in grace alone of the resurrection, into His kingdom, was the promise that faith was placed in. Without works. *To him that worketh not.* That this election of grace applies to the Gentile as much as the Jew. That there is no difference between Jew and the Greek, that if all are condemned, then all are saved in Jesus if they believe. It's flawless doctrine, relentlessly building on itself.

Here in Romans 11 Paul is finishing the thought of what to say about the physical Israel, the Jews, given all this doctrine. What does the Gospel of Christ mean pertaining to the old covenant? (God is a logical God, who wants us to *reason together* with Him)

Dispensationalism rests primarily on vs 1-5, and, like most bad doctrine, isolating verses out of context to achieve it. They say "see, God's not done with Israel!"

But here Paul specifically is offering himself as the example, that the remnant is those who believe the Gospel. For we know from the prior chapters that there is a conditional state to salvation, belief. Obeying the Gospel. And so any Jew who believes will be that remnant. Same as the Greek who are grafted in to the promise by their faith.

Verse 6 has God hammer again the point that salvation is not by works. It is 100% by faith, least it no more be of grace. Because it is a gift and the rewards for work is a debt owed. (Works-nibbas BTHO, again)

So, having established that the Jews after the flesh have to believe, Paul circles back to Romans 1 and reprobate doctrine, calling in mind the imprecatory prayer of David to blind the wicked who reject the truth of God, unto damnation.

However, Paul prays that the Gentiles receiving the blessing and promises, being grafted in, provoked his kinsmen to repentance. That they turn from stubborn unbelief to accepting the Gospel. That they who are believe would be sent, preaching the word, and by hearing, physical Israel believe and be grafted in again. That by his own example living for Christ he gets his nation to want to emulate him and be saved.

This plea is a familiar lament to many Christians. We all have unsaved relatives, often close. Friends, coworkers. People for whom we earnestly pray accept the free gift of salvation but who have hardened their hearts.

Paul's example of being worthy of emulation is a model for us, that we live the Gospel in a way that draws them to the light and softens their hearts that they may be willing to believe.

The warning to Gentiles against becoming arrogant regarding their position relative to grace and the reprobate silver nation of Jews should also be taken to heart.

A Godly nation can easily turn from the truth and be burned in the fire, just as easily as recalcitrant Israel could have a revival in Christ and be graft back in. Prodigals restored as heirs.

Dispies falsely make this an unconditional statement rather than an argument; that Jews **will** be graft in regardless of their own belief or wickedness.

Paul has built his case, in the Spirit, that everything here is contingent on believing God's law and promises, whom all men know, and knowing are condemned without excuse, except they believe in the gospel, which is of faith in Christ's crucifixion and resurrection for the remission of all sins, that this is a gift available to everyone, without works, entirely of grace, but that God doesn't hold it out to be taken indefinitely, and that at some point He will cut off the unbelieving, reject and turn them over to reprobation. Individual salvation to eternal life, or a physical nation on earth, it's the same.

teachings.title: To your tents, O Israel
teachings.summary: Israel's rebellion against Rehoboam in 1 Kings 12 pictures the Jews rejecting Christ, and every man going to his own house in John 7 is its parallel.
teachings.text:
Every man went to his own house, the matter unresolved, reminds me of the verse in **1 Kings 12:16**:

*So when all Israel saw that the king hearkened not unto them, the people answered the king, saying, What portion have we in David? neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: to your tents, O Israel: now see to thine own house, David. So Israel departed unto their tents.*

In this account of the old kingdom being divided, between the northern tribes and Judah we see the people demanding that Solomon's son, Rehoboam who has just been anointed king, ease the enforcement of God's law, claiming it's too heavy a yoke to bear. They rebel, they kill the man sent by Rehoboam to collect tribute (picturing God the Father sending Jesus, and the Jews killing Him). They then name Jeroboam their king, (picturing men putting their faith in what they want, rather than what God tells us).

*So Israel rebelled against the house of David unto this day.*..

This rejection led to God's wrath upon the northern kingdom, and their having renounced their inheritance, their portion of the promise in David, they were eradicated by the Assyrians.

This is a picture of the Jews in Jesus' day, some choosing to follow God's anointed, most choosing their own way, and thus divided, each returns to their own house to do as they will.

*O Israel, return to thy tents*, and *every man went unto his own house,* shows that this is a parallel passage.

teachings.title: Sons of the freewoman, not the bondwoman
teachings.summary: Believers are adopted heirs freed from the tutors of the law, and as Isaac and Ishmael show, those born of the Spirit inherit while those under the bondage of works are cast out.
teachings.text:
Building upon the doctrine that we who believe God are adopted by God, sons according to the promise; being heirs. Continuing that thought, Paul makes the comparison of the law vs grace, that the son can be heir but under a schoolmaster, tutors and governors, yet in the fullness of time, be as the Lord, an inheritor of all. So to, he's saying, the Israelites were when under the law, children of the promise, not come into their inheritance. Now, with the fullness of Christ, all who believe are adopted and freed from the burden of the law, of the tutors and governess, to their inheritance.

Paul explaining this in these terms, as laid out in Hebrew scripture that they may understand, given there are Jews pushing the Galatians to go back under that bondage. Paul says he's afraid of the Galatians that they may be so easily led to a false gospel, that he questions if they even were saved. That we who believe have the Spirit of the Son within us. That we have that quickened spirit, born again crying "Abba!"(Father) to God. They should know better. They should recognize the error. Yet they don't, and so Paul has to assume his labor in preaching the Gospel of grace was in vain, that they aren't saved.

He reminds them that before his preaching the word to them, they served idols, living as heathens, and these judaizers come in and return them to superstition, marking sabbaths and holy days done away with in Christ. Returning them to the bondage of works based salvation.

He reminds them of when he was present with them, the zeal for the Gospel they held, that in spite of a physical infirmity, apparently with Paul's eyes, they readily accepted him to the point they'd have plucked out their own eyes to right his. But now he's their enemy for telling them the truth. He compares winning them to Christ with travails of a mother in birth, and says he's willing to do it to bring them to salvation.

Changing gears, and having established that our salvation is one of adoption, blessing and inheritance from the Father, he asks those who are going back to the OT if they even know it, and uses an example from the Law, the story of Isaac and Ihsmael. How, as told in Genesis 17, Abraham had a son, Ishmael, with a slave woman, Hagar, by natural means, and Isaac with his wife Sara, by spiritual means. When Issac was still an infant, Ishmael teased him, and Sara demanded Abraham to kick Hagar and the boy out, denying him any share of inheritance.

Thus we who are born again in the Spirit become heirs, while those trying to work their way into the kingdom, those under bondage, are denied.

*Now we, brethren, as Isaac was, are the children of promise.*

And, again as Ishmael the son of the flesh persecuted Isaac, son of the Spirit, so to now the Jews after the flesh are misleading them, persecuting the heirs in Christ.

*Nevertheless what saith the scripture? Cast out the bondwoman and her son: for the son of the bondwoman shall not be heir with the son of the freewoman. So then, brethren, we are not children of the bondwoman, but of the free.*

teachings.title: By grace are ye saved through faith
teachings.summary: Jew and Gentile alike were children of wrath and are saved only by grace through faith, not works, made one new man in Christ with the partition removed.
teachings.text:
Ephesians chapter 1 built the theme of the first 3 chapters; the promise of God, predestinated in Christ and redeemed in us through faith, to be heirs to His Kingdom, and being bestowed with spiritual blessings as His sons.

The immediate application of this for the Galatians and other Gentiles to whom it is written was the Jews attitude towards them, even in the early church. That they were not joint heirs. That they were somehow less than believing Jews in the Kingdom of Heaven, not having been of the "chosen people."

It's one of the reasons for Paul's emphasis on being elect in Christ. Being all chosen to members of the body of which Jesus is the head.

Here in chapter 2, Paul builds on the idea of adoption of grace, to being sons of God, and compares the sonship of believers to the 'children of disobedience,' or the 'children of wrath.' which we all were, Jew or Gentile, without grace from God, His mercy and the blood of Christ, that we who believe are quickened, our spirit born again as His sons.

Even when we were dead in sins, Christ died for us all. That we may sit *together,* raised up *together,* by the grace and mercy of God. Something we all needed to be there, Jew or Gentile. *Together* in Christ. And all bestowed with blessings of the exceeding richness of our Father, given by God's grace.

*For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast.*

Grace is unmerited, unearned and unconditional love. Things given in grace are given not because of anything we have done or who we are, by by faith in Christ, God's gift is made accessible to us all.

Not of circumcision of the flesh, or the law of commandments contained in ordinances. But by grace through faith in God's mercy and Jesus' blood shed for the word.

Paul acknowledges that at times, before Christ, that the Gentiles were "afar off," kept in twain, ignorant of the law and of the promise. But now, *made nigh by the blood of Christ.*

The partition between peoples and who were elect by grace through faith, removed after the coming of Jesus. All saved become a new man. *For through him we both have access by one Spirit unto the Father.*

No more strangers or foreigners, we are all made part of the temple of God, with Jesus as the cornerstone, the foundation laid by the prophets and apostles. Each believer, a pillar.

teachings.title: This generation shall not pass
teachings.summary: This generation means the generation that sees the signs, not merely the first century or the Jews, and Christ's word that their house is left desolate shows God's wrath on the unbelieving Jews.
teachings.text:
As for the verse following the parable of the fig tree, **Matthew 24:34**, which gives so many trouble;

*Verily I say unto you, This generation shall not pass, till all these things be fulfilled.*

Jesus has just laid out future prophecy, written to us as much as to the Apostles to whom he preached. (Again, the false doctrine of dispensationalism teaches that this is directed at the Jews, who weren't present and who Jesus refers to as "they," as others, while referring to we, ye the believers, making their interpretation nonsensical.)

So Jesus is preaching of the future generation, present at the time of these signs. Who are reading the times as one could read the fig tree in its due season. This is that generation, which we may be under, or our great grandchildren for that matter. But once the timing of things is made clear to those keeping watch, prepared for the master's return, that generation will not pass until all those things be revealed.

There is dual fulfillment as well, obviously, that the generation of 1st century believers would live to see the destruction in 70AD, but that is not the context of what's given, and those who seek to make it about that have to do contortions to make it fit their doctrine, that the end times is entirely about the Jews.

"God is not finished with the Jews!" Really? In the chapter previous, **Matthew 23**, just before Jesus leaving the temple at the start of this private discourse on Olivette to the apostles, Christ makes it known in no uncertain terms:

*O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not! Behold, your house is left unto you desolate. For I say unto you, Ye shall not see me henceforth, till ye shall say, Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.*

He was through preaching to them that believed not and rejected Him as they rejected the prophets that came before Him. God's wrath abides upon them to the uttermost. From that day forth, an accursed and wicked generation of men.

But they are correct about one thing, God isn't through with them yet. And the Days of Vengeance they who remain, that Synagogue of Satan, will be utterly destroyed.

teachings.title: The wicked husbandmen given over
teachings.summary: In the parable of the vineyard Jesus shows the Jews who knew the truth yet sought to kill Him, so God gave them over to a reprobate mind and will destroy them and give the kingdom to others, contrary to dispensationalism.
teachings.text:
Following the story of the fig tree which Jesus cursed for not producing fruit, He tells a parable. The master leaving a vineyard to be tended sends for the gathering, and the husbandmen he'd entrusted with the land beat and kill his messengers. He sends his only begotten son and they plot to kill him and take the inheritance for themselves.

With this not so thinly veiled analogy, Jesus puts the Jews who are seeking to kill Him on notice. They discern that Jesus is talking about them. Unlike most of His parables that fell on deaf ears. The Bible says "*they knew that he had spoken the parable against them: and they left him, and went their way*."

It is amazing to us who believe that there are those who knowing the truth, seek to silence it, even with the Son of the Lord standing there in their presence. Even with the history of the Jews, who killed the prophets of God, and now plot to do the same to Christ.

They wish to not retain the word of God and the truth of Christ in their knowledge. They sought instead to take the inheritance of an earthly kingdom for themselves by His death. They worship the creation more than the creator. And God turned them over, gave them up, to a reprobate mind to do those things which are inconvenient.

*Reprobate silver men shall call them.*

Again, the dispensationalist idea that the Jews held a special place and God wasn't through with them yet, is a lie. They were given the advantage of the oracles of God and the ministry of Jesus Christ in the flesh, and rather than repent towards God, they sought to destroy Him.

And like the master of the vineyard, *he will come and destroy the husbandmen, and will give the vineyard unto others.*

It does not say He will take it from them for a time. He destroys them and gives the Kingdom to those who will produce fruit, giving God the increase, in His Son's name.

teachings.title: Reprobate silver: a national identity
teachings.summary: Quoting Romans 1:18-32 and Jeremiah 6:30, he teaches that the Jews who rejected the Messiah are reprobate by their individual free will and collectively judged, so that it is their national identity.
teachings.text:
**Romans 1:18-32**

*Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools,*
*And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things.*

*Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves:*
*Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.*

*For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature: And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet.*
*And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient; Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers, Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful: Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them.*

Speaking specifically of the Jews who would reject the coming Messiah;

**Jeremiah 6:30**

*Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the Lord hath rejected them.*

It is their national identity. By their individual free will. Collectively judged.

teachings.title: Sarah's life an allegory of believing Israel
teachings.summary: Sarah's life pictures faithful Old Testament Israel saved by faith in the promise, while Hagar and Ishmael picture Israel after the flesh, cast out.
teachings.text:
Now, as the Bible in **Galatians 4** says, regarding the story of Sarah and Isaac, that these things be an allegory, the children of the promise in Sarah, the children after the bondage of the law, in Hagar. That the true seed of Abraham isn't after the flesh, as Ishmael was by the bondwoman Hagar, but by the miracle of God, Issac, conceived in faith through Sarah.

The life story of Sarah represents Old Testament Israel, faithful believing Israel, who were saved through faith in the promise made to Abraham. An allegory, as the Bible says.

When we first meet Sarah, as a young wife to Abraham, we are told she was barren. Without hope of conception. She journeys to Canaan, the promised land.

Later, due to famine, she sojourns into Egypt, is captured by Pharaoh, and God for Sarah's sake visits plagues upon the Pharoah's house until he relents and sends Sarah, Abraham, Lot and their cattle and belongings out from Egypt. Just as the Israelites spoiled Egypt, and went out with them, a mixed multitude.

Sarah, despite her faith and love of God lapses in faith, and brings adultery to the bed of Abraham, with Hagar. Sarah's impatience with God's promise has her seek to find an heir after the flesh. Just as the Israelites lapsed in faith and brought the adultery of strange gods at times, and eventually sought an earthly king to rule them, frustrated at the timing of God.

And like Israel, which would at times repent and turn back to God, admitting their error, Sarah says to Abraham; *My wrong be upon thee: I have given my maid into thy bosom; and when she saw that she had conceived, I was despised in her eyes: the Lord judge between me and thee.*

And Hagar, having fled from Sarah with Ishmael the heir after the law, representing Israel after the flesh, not of faith, was given another chance by God, so too were the Jews of Jesus earthly ministry, to receive the adoption by faith that they though was theirs by law. And Sarah, believing Israel, gave them a home until the coming of Isaac.

We are told of another captivity, Sarah taken by a king, and freed not by plagues but by the fear of the Lord upon Abimelech, convicted of his error, just as Babylonian captivity was.

And when Isaac was born, Ishmael mocked the heir of the promise, and Sarah cast out the bondwoman and her son, though it grieved Abraham, the father. But God agrees with Sarah that son after the flesh, the heir according to the law be cast out, so that the son of faith may come in to his inheritance in full. Just as the non-believing Jews were cut off.

(God, in His mercy offers salvation to Hagar if she just believe. And a well of water giving her salvation, just as any seed of Abraham after the flesh can still repent towards Christ today)

Finally, Sarah having seen her son born of a miracle and come to be offered as a sacrifice, (I believe at 33 upon a hill in Jerusalem, spared by God, a picture of Jesus) she passes away a year later, at 127 years old and is honored, being given a place with the patriarchs, our being told of her end, chronicled by scripture. And in her faith, she was saved, and through her, all nations and kindreds were blessed.

teachings.title: Jacob have I loved, Esau have I hated
teachings.summary: The hatred of Esau refers to the later wicked nation of Edom, not to Esau himself, who God blessed and who was saved by faith, against the Calvinist reading.
teachings.text:
He is Esau who is Edom. He is Esau the father of the Edomites.

We are given the genealogies of Esau, who is Edom, which God repeats for us several times, to drive home the point.

The primary target for this scripture were the Israelites in Moses day, sharing their people's story and the story of the people of Mt Seir, who they are coming up against as we will see later in scripture. Cousins really. One with the blessing and the promise for the seed that is Christ to come.

Esau himself is often painted in a negative light, primarily due to a Calvinist reading of **Romans 9:13**:

*As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.*

Which is itself taken from the prophet **Malachi 1:3-4**

*And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness. Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places; thus saith the Lord of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever. And your eyes shall see, and ye shall say, The Lord will be magnified from the border of Israel.*

Note, these are the Edomites generations later, being cursed by God. Not Esau, who is Edom.

And why were they cursed by God for destruction? In **Deuteronomy 2:1-5**, God orders the Israelites to tread carefully through the land of Seir so as not to worry the Edomites. That their land was promised Esau:

*Then we turned, and took our journey into the wilderness by the way of the Red sea, as the Lord spake unto me: and we compassed mount Seir many days.*

*And the Lord spake unto me, saying,*
*Ye have compassed this mountain long enough: turn you northward.*
*And command thou the people, saying, Ye are to pass through the coast of your brethren the children of Esau, which dwell in Seir; and they shall be afraid of you: take ye good heed unto yourselves therefore: Meddle not with them; for I will not give you of their land, no, not so much as a foot breadth; because I have given mount Seir unto Esau for a possession.*

We see at this point God is still allowing the nations of Edom, who is Esau to continue with His blessing of a promised land to their patriarch.

God loved Esau, despite his failings. He made a promise to him and kept it, even in those days, 400yrs later.

Esau was saved by the same faith as Jacob, and their fathers. But his descendents became wicked.

**Numbers 20:14-21**

*And Moses sent messengers from Kadesh unto the king of Edom, Thus saith thy brother Israel, Thou knowest all the travail that hath befallen us:*
*How our fathers went down into Egypt, and we have dwelt in Egypt a long time; and the Egyptians vexed us, and our fathers: And when we cried unto the Lord, he heard our voice, and sent an angel, and hath brought us forth out of Egypt: and, behold, we are in Kadesh, a city in the uttermost of thy border:*

*Let us pass, I pray thee, through thy country: we will not pass through the fields, or through the vineyards, neither will we drink of the water of the wells: we will go by the king's high way, we will not turn to the right hand nor to the left, until we have passed thy borders.*

*And Edom said unto him, Thou shalt not pass by me, lest I come out against thee with the sword. And the children of Israel said unto him, We will go by the high way: and if I and my cattle drink of thy water, then I will pay for it: I will only, without doing anything else, go through on my feet.*

*And he said, Thou shalt not go through. And Edom came out against him with much people, and with a strong hand. Thus Edom refused to give Israel passage through his border: wherefore Israel turned away from him.*

Later we see Edomites war with Israel, and eventually David conquers and takes them as servants, slaves.

**2 Samuel 8:13-14**

teachings.title: Joseph's Brothers Hated Him as the Jews Hated Christ
teachings.summary: The brothers' resentment of Joseph's prophetic dreams mirrors the Jews' hatred of Christ, of whom Moses and the prophets wrote.
teachings.text:
And so, we understand the setting. They hate the favoritism Jacob gives his son, Joseph and that he's tattled on their sin. *They hated him, and could not speak peaceably unto him*, and to compound matters, Joseph tells them of his dream.

*For, behold, we were binding sheaves in the field, and, lo, my sheaf arose, and also stood upright; and, behold, your sheaves stood round about, and made obeisance to my sheaf.*
*And his brethren said to him, Shalt thou indeed reign over us? or shalt thou indeed have dominion over us? And they hated him yet the more for his dreams, and for his words.*

In parallel to Christ, we see the resentment. Like Jews resentment of Christians, the older hating the younger because of the prophecy of who will reign. Not exact but echos. And Joseph dreams again.
